{{Infobox ancient site |name = Nishitonozuka Kofun |image = [[File:Nishitonotsuka Kofun, zenkei.jpg|280px]]
Full view of the mound (front section on the right, rear circle in the back left) |Group = {{ill|Yamato Kofun Group|ja|大和古墳群|1=Ōyamato Kofun Group}} (Nakayama subgroup) |location = {{ill|Tenri, Nara Prefecture|ja|天理市}}, Nakayama Town, Nishitonozuka{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳（古墳）|1989}} |LatitudeDegrees = 34|LatitudeMinutes = 34|LatitudeSeconds = 6.22 |LongitudeDegrees = 135|LongitudeMinutes = 51|LongitudeSeconds = 4.26 |ISO = JP-29 |Type = {{ill|Keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳}} |Scale = Mound length approximately 230{{ill|Meters|ja|メートル}}
Height approximately 16m (rear circle) |Construction = Late {{ill|3rd century|ja|3世紀}} to its end |BurialFacility = Unknown |Interred = ({{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} designation) {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|ja|手白香皇女}}
(One theory) {{ill|Queen Himiko|ja|台与}}
(Another theory) Emperor {{ill|Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}} |Artifacts = {{ill|Special pedestal and pottery|ja|特殊器台・特殊壺}}, Miyama-style special pedestals and pottery
Ordinary cylindrical haniwa |Mausoleum = {{ill|Fusumada Mausoleum|ja|衾田陵}} (designated by the Imperial Household Agency) |Notes = Ranked 24th nationwide by size
(if mound length is considered 219m)[https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/ranking/zenkoku.html Ranking of Tumulus Sizes in Japan] (Sakai City website, updated May 13, 2018).
Considered the royal tomb following {{ill|Hashihaka Kofun|ja|箸墓古墳}} |Map = Japan Nara |Label = Nishitonozuka Kofun |LabelPosition = Top |Icon = Keyhole-shaped tomb - South }} [[File:Nishitonotsuka Kofun, haisho.jpg|thumb|220px|{{center|{{ill|Princess Tashiraka|ja|手白香皇女}} Fusumada Mausoleum Worship Site}}]] '''Nishitonozuka Kofun''' (西殿塚古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in {{ill|Tenri, Nara Prefecture|ja|天理市}}, Nakayama Town. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳}} and part of the {{ill|Yamato Kofun Group|ja|大和古墳群|1=Ōyamato Kofun Group}} (Nakayama subgroup). The identity of the interred is uncertain, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} designates the site as the '''Fusumada Mausoleum''' (衾田陵), the resting place of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|ja|手白香皇女}}, the consort of [[Emperor Keitai]] It is estimated to have been built in the latter half of the {{ill|3rd century|ja|3世紀}} (early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}) and is considered the royal tomb succeeding the earliest keyhole-shaped tomb, the {{ill|Hashihaka Kofun|ja|箸墓古墳}}. == Overview == It is a gigantic keyhole-shaped tumulus constructed on the hilly area along the eastern edge of the {{ill|Nara Basin|ja|奈良盆地}}. Adjacent to its eastern side is the {{ill|Higashitonotsuka Kofun|ja|東殿塚古墳|1=Higashitonotsuka Kofun}}, and these two, being at the highest point within the {{ill|Yamato Kofun Group|ja|大和古墳群|1=Ōyamato Kofun Group}}, offer a panoramic view of the entire basinHistoric Site Explanation Board.{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 陵墓篇 第65号|2014|pp=108-112}}. The tumulus has remained well preserved to the present day{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991|pp=100-111}}. It is currently managed by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as the mausoleum of an empress under its jurisdiction; to date, exterior investigations of the tumulus have been conducted by the {{ill|Archives and Mausolea Department|ja|宮内庁書陵部}} during the {{ill|1989|ja|1989年}} ({{ill|Heisei|ja|平成}} first fiscal year) period{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991|pp=100-111}}, surveys of the surrounding area by the Tenri City Board of Education during the {{ill|1992|ja|1992年|lt=1992|lt_ja=1992年}}–{{ill|1994|ja|1994年}} period (Heisei 4–6 fiscal years){{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=1-4}}, and an academic on-site survey in the {{ill|2012|ja|2012年}} period (Heisei 24 fiscal year){{R|2013年調査}}. The tumulus is of a keyhole shape with its anterior portion facing south; however, because it was constructed at a right angle to a sloping terrain (with the higher elevation on the east side), it takes on an asymmetrical form{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}. In the posterior circular portion, it is built with three tiers on the east side and four tiers on the west side, while in the anterior portion it is built with one tier on the east side and two tiers on the west side{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=5-7}}. The overall length of the tumulus measures about 230 {{ill|meters|ja|メートル}}, making it the largest within the Yamato Kofun Group. On its exterior, in addition to the presence of {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}}, early haniwa have been detected around the tumulus, including {{ill|Special platforms and jars|ja|特殊器台・特殊壺|lt=Special Kiderai-type earthenware, special Kiderai-type haniwa, special tsubo-shaped haniwa|lt_ja=特殊器台形土器・特殊器台形埴輪・特殊壺形埴輪}} (from the tumulus itself) and {{ill|Cylindrical Haniwa|ja|円筒埴輪|lt=cylindrical haniwa}} with a stepped neck{{R|説明板}}. Although the burial facilities remain unclear, square platforms (mounds) are present on both the posterior and anterior portions of the tumulus{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=5-7}}. This Nishitonozuka Kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the latter half of the {{ill|3rd century|ja|3世紀}} during the early part of the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}{{R|説明板}}[http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/miryoku/tenrinomiryoku1/kofun/1445323092951.html]{{ill|Nishitonozuka Kofun|ja|西殿塚古墳}} (Tenri City Homepage). It is regarded as the great tomb of the Yamato Kingdom that succeeded the {{ill|Hashihaka Kofun|ja|箸墓古墳}} (located in {{ill|Sakurai City|ja|桜井市}} Hashinaka){{R|白石}}, and in conjunction with the adjacent {{ill|Higaida-ōtsuka Kofun|ja|東殿塚古墳|1=Higashitonotsuka Kofun}}, it is considered to be part of a continuous construction sequence beginning with Nishitonozuka Kofun{{R|説明板}}. Although the identity of the interred remains unclear, it is currently designated by the Imperial Household Agency as the mausoleum of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|lt=Tebarakakōjo|ja|手白香皇女}} (the {{ill|Empress|ja|皇后}} of the 26th {{ill|Emperor Keitai|ja|継体天皇}} ){{Sfn|衾田陵（国史）}}. However, since the construction date does not correspond with the assumed period of the {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} for {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|lt=Tebarakakōjo|ja|手白香皇女}}, a theory that the true mausoleum of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|lt=Tebarakakōjo|ja|手白香皇女}} is the {{ill|Nishiyamazuka Kofun|ja|西山塚古墳}} (in Tenri City, Kayashō Town) is strongly supported{{Sfn|天理の古墳100|2015|p=55}}, while alternative theories propose that the true interred of this tumulus is {{ill|Toyo (queen)|ja|台与|lt=Queen Toyo}}, a successor to {{ill|Himiko|ja|卑弥呼}} (who may have been enshrined in the Hashihaka Kofun){{R|白石}}. [[category:New pages]][[ja:西殿塚古墳]] == Burial == The interred individual is not definitively known, but the site is officially designated as the resting place of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|ja|手白香皇女}}. However, the construction date (3rd century) conflicts with Princess Tashiraka’s presumed era (6th century), leading some to propose the nearby {{ill|Nishiyamazuka Kofun|ja|西山塚古墳}} as her true mausoleum.{{Sfn|天理の古墳100|2015|p=55}} Other theories suggest Queen {{ill|Himiko|ja|卑弥呼}}’s successor, {{ill|Toyo (queen)|ja|台与|lt=Queen Toyo}}, or [[Emperor Sujin]] as the interred individual.{{Sfn|白石太一郎|2013|pp=171-174}} == Site History == * {{ill|1876|ja|1876年}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治}} 9), designated as the mausoleum of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|lt=Tebarakakōjo|ja|手白香皇女}}{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 陵墓篇 第65号|2014|pp=108-112}}. * {{ill|1889|ja|1889年}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治}} 22), repaired and maintained as a mausoleum {{ill|Kinuta Tomb|ja|衾田陵（国史）}}. * {{ill|1986|ja|1986年}} period ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和}} 61 fiscal year), the first survey was conducted{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=1-4}}. * {{ill|1989|ja|1989年}} period ({{ill|Heisei|ja|平成}} first fiscal year), an exterior survey of the tumulus was carried out by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency Shoryo Department|ja|宮内庁書陵部}} {{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991|pp=100-111}}. * From {{ill|1992|ja|1992年|lt=1992|lt_ja=1992}} to {{ill|1994|ja|1994年}}, ({{ill|Heisei|ja|平成}} 4–6 fiscal years), the 2nd to 4th surveys were conducted by the Tenri City Board of Education{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=1-4}}. * {{ill|2012|ja|2012年}} ({{ill|Heisei|ja|平成}} 24): ** On April 9, an aerial 3D survey was conducted by the {{ill|Nara Prefectural Kashihara Archaeological Institute|ja|奈良県立橿原考古学研究所}} and {{ill|Asia Aerial Surveying|ja|アジア航測}}{{PDFlink|[http://www.ajiko.co.jp/news/2012/hashihaka_rittaichizu.pdf "Creation of a Red-colored 3D Map of the Hashihaka and Seidenzuka Kofun"]}} (Press release from the Nara Prefectural Kashihara Archaeological Institute and Asia Aerial Surveying Co., Ltd., 2012).[https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXNASDG0503K_V00C12A6CR8000/ "Himiko’s Tomb? 3D Helicopter Survey of the Hashihaka Kofun by Kashihara Institute, etc."] (Nikkei, June 5, 2012).. ** In August, following a theft incident (with no destruction of the remains) and subsequent restoration, a survey was carried out by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency Shoryo Department|ja|宮内庁書陵部}} {{Sfn|書陵部紀要 陵墓篇 第65号|2014|pp=108-112}}. * {{ill|2013|ja|2013年}} ({{ill|Heisei|ja|平成}} 25) on February 20, an on-site survey was conducted by representatives of 15 academic societies in archaeology and history[https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXNASDG1905C_Q3A220C1CR0000/ "Himiko’s Tomb? First On-site Survey at the Hashihaka Kofun in Nara, Raising Expectations for Research Progress"] (Nikkei, February 20, 2013).. == Tumulus == [[File:Tonotono-tsuka stereo.jpg|thumb|{{center|Nishitonozuka Kofun's {{ill|Stereogram|ja|ステレオグラム|lt=Stereogram|lt_ja=ステレオ}} Aerial Photograph (1979) In the image, the {{ill|Higashidenzuka Kofun|ja|東殿塚古墳|1=Higashitonotsuka Kofun}} is shown at the top and the {{ill|Seidenzuka Kofun|ja|西殿塚古墳|1=Nishitonozuka Kofun}} at the bottom. {{ill|National Aerial Photography|ja|国土航空写真}}.]] The dimensions of the tumulus are as follows{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=5-7}}. * Tumulus length: approximately 230 meters (in some sources, 234 meters{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}, 220 meters{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 陵墓篇 第65号|2014|pp=108-112}}, or 219 meters{{R|堺市}}). * Posterior circular portion – built with 3 tiers on the east side and 4 tiers on the west side. ** Diameter: approximately 140 meters ** Height: approximately 16 meters (east side) * Anterior portion – built with 1 tier on the east side and 2 tiers on the west side. ** Width: approximately 130 meters ** Height: approximately 12 meters (east side) * Square platform (mound) – built in one tier. ** Posterior circular portion: 25.15 meters east–west, 26.54 meters north–south, height 3.00 meters{{R|2012年報道発表資料}} ** Anterior portion: 12.92 meters east–west, 14.43 meters north–south, height 1.87 meters{{R|2012年報道発表資料}} In the theory where the tumulus length is taken as 219 meters, it ranks as the 24th largest in the country{{R|堺市}}. The tiered terraces of the tumulus do not directly connect the posterior circular and anterior portions; the difference in tiers between these portions is reconciled in the constricted section{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991|pp=100-111}}. Furthermore, on the western side of the tumulus, a broad, flat surface (apron), characteristic of the Nishitonozuka Kofun, has been shaped as the lowest tier{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=5-7}}. On the eastern side of the tumulus, there are two bridge-like structures located in the central area of the posterior circular portion and on the southern side of the anterior portion, both of which connect to the adjacent {{ill|Higashidenzuka Kofun|ja|東殿塚古墳|1=Higashitonotsuka Kofun}}{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=5-7}}. == Interred ==
'''Family Tree Based on the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}}'''The reign information is based on the {{ill|Nihon Jinmei Daijiten|ja|日本人名大辞典}} (Kodansha). {{familytree/start|style="text-align:left; font-size:100%"}} {{familytree|border=0|||||01| 01={{sup|24}} {{ill|Emperor Ninken|ja|仁賢天皇}}
{{small|(Reign: end of 5th century)}}}} {{familytree|border=0|||||||)|.}} {{familytree|border=0|01|y|02|03| 01={{sup|26}} {{ill|Emperor Keitai|ja|継体天皇}}
{{small|(Reign: 507?-531?)}}|02={{ill|Princess Tashiraka|lt=Tebarakakōjo|ja|手白香皇女}}|03={{sup|25}} {{ill|Emperor Buretsu|ja|武烈天皇}}
{{small|(Reign: end of 5th century – early 6th century)}}}} {{familytree|border=0||||01|| 01={{sup|29}} {{ill|Emperor Kinmei|ja|欽明天皇}}
{{small|(Reign: 539?-571?)}}}} {{familytree/end}}
The actual interred of the {{ill|Seidenzuka Kofun|ja|西殿塚古墳|1=Nishitonozuka Kofun}} remains unclear; however, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} designates it as the mausoleum of the 26th {{ill|Emperor Keitai|ja|継体天皇}}’s consort, '''{{ill|Princess Tashiraka|lt=Tebarakakōjo|ja|手白香皇女}}''' (Tashiraka no Hime-miko, also rendered as Tashiraka no Hairarō/ Tashiraka no Himemi){{Sfn|衾田陵（国史）}}Compiled by the Imperial Ministry of Mausolea [{{NDLDC|1237123/11}} "Guide to Mausolea"] (1934, National Diet Library Digital Collection), 11 panels."Compilation of Mausoleum Topographical Maps, Abbreviated Edition", compiled by the Imperial Household Agency Shoryo Department Mausoleum Section, [[Gakuseisha]], 2014, p. 406.. Although the mausoleum of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|lt=Tebarakakōjo|ja|手白香皇女}} is not mentioned in either the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} or the {{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}}, in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}’s mausolea section (displayed as {{ill|Shoryo Department|ja|諸陵寮}}) it is recorded as the distant "Kinuta Tomb". It is said to be located in {{ill|Yamato Province|ja|大和国}}’s {{ill|Yamabe District|ja|山辺郡}}, covering an area of two chō east–west and two chō north–south, with no separate guard door, the mound door of the Kamikami Burial Mound of Yamabe (the mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Sushin|ja|崇神天皇}}) concurrently serving as its guard{{Sfn|衾田陵（国史）}}. Later, during the {{ill|Medieval period|ja|中世}}, the traditional accounts regarding the location of the mausoleum were lost{{Sfn|衾田陵（国史）}}. In {{ill|1876|ja|1876年}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治}} 9), the {{ill|Kyōbushō|ja|教部省}} designated the {{ill|Seidenzuka Kofun|ja|西殿塚古墳|1=Nishitonozuka Kofun}} as the mausoleum, and in {{ill|1889|ja|1889年}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治}} 22) repairs were carried out{{Sfn|衾田陵（国史）}}. [[File:Hashihaka-kofun zenkei.JPG|サムネイル|220px|{{center|{{ill|Hashihaka Kofun|ja|箸墓古墳}} (located in {{ill|Sakurai City|ja|桜井市}}, Hashinaka)}}{{small|Attributed to {{ill|Wajishiki no Hime|ja|倭迹迹日百襲姫命}}. Archaeologically, it is considered either the tomb of the first great king of the {{ill|Yamato Kingdom|ja|ヤマト王権}} or the tomb of {{ill|Himiko|ja|卑弥呼}}.}}]] On the other hand, regarding the true mausoleum of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|lt=Tebarakakōjo|ja|手白香皇女}}, a prevailing theory holds that it should be identified not with the Nishitonozuka Kofun but with the {{ill|Nishiyamazuka Kofun|ja|西山塚古墳}} (located in Tenri City, Kayashō Town){{Sfn|天理の古墳100|2015|p=55}}. This theory is based on the fact that while the construction date of the Nishitonozuka Kofun is estimated to be around the latter half of the 3rd century, the date for the Nishiyamazuka Kofun is around the {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}}, which corresponds with the assumed period for {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|lt=Tebarakakōjo|ja|手白香皇女}}{{Sfn|天理の古墳100|2015|p=55}}. Meanwhile, as for the true interred of the Nishitonozuka Kofun, some theories propose that it is {{ill|Daiyo|ja|台与}} (also written 壹與/臺與), based on its subsequent position to the {{ill|Hashihaka Kofun|ja|箸墓古墳}}—regarded as the tomb of {{ill|Himiko|ja|卑弥呼}}—or that it is {{ill|Emperor Sushin|ja|崇神天皇}}{{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, ''The Formation and Development of the Wa Kingdom as Seen from the Kofun'', Keibunsha, 2013, pp. 171-174.,{{ill|Suiz Wada|ja|和田萃}} “On the Yamabe Road”, in ''The Ancient History of Mount Miwa'', Gakuseisha, 2003. among others. {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%" |+ Estimated Early Great King Tombs of the Yamato Kingdom
{{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, ''The Formation and Development of the Wa Kingdom as Seen from the Kofun'' (日本歴史 私の最新講義), Keibunsha, 2013, pp. 181-186. ! Order !! Tumulus Name |- |1||{{ill|Hashihaka Kofun|ja|箸墓古墳}} |- |2||'''{{ill|Nishitonozuka Kofun|ja|西殿塚古墳|1=Nishitonozuka Kofun}}''' |- |3||{{ill|Sakurai Chausuyama Kofun|ja|桜井茶臼山古墳|lt=Sakurai Chausuyama Kofun|lt_ja=外山茶臼山古墳}} |- |4||{{ill|Mesuriyama Kofun|ja|メスリ山古墳}} |- |5||{{ill|Andonyama Kofun|ja|行燈山古墳}} |- |6||{{ill|Shibuya Mukaeyama Kofun|ja|渋谷向山古墳}} |} == References == {{Reflist|2}} == Further Reading == * Site explanation board, Tenri City Board of Education, 2010. * {{Cite book|和書|title=Nishitonozuka Kofun and Higashitonozuka Kofun (Tenri City Cultural Heritage Report No.7)|publisher=Tenri City Board of Education|year=2000|ref={{Harvid|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|title=100 Kofun in Tenri|publisher=Tenri City Board of Education|year=2015|ref={{Harvid|天理の古墳100|2015}}}} == Related Articles == * {{ill|Yamato Kofun Group|ja|大和古墳群|1=Ōyamato Kofun Group}} * {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|ja|手白香皇女}} == External Links == * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/miryoku/tenrinomiryoku1/kofun/1445323092951.html Nishitonozuka Kofun - Tenri City website] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Yamato Kofun Group]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Nara Prefecture]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:History of Tenri]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Imperial Tombs of Japan]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]] [[Category:kk]] [[Category:Fixed Kofun templates]] {{Kofun navbar}} [[Category:Fixed Kofun templates]] [[Category:kk]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:Nishitonozuka Kofun]][[Category:kk]] [[Category:qq]][[Category:Nishitonozuka Kofun]][[Category:qq]] [[ja:西殿塚古墳]] [[Category:new pages]] [[Category:大和古墳群]] [[Category:前方後円墳]][[sn:Nishitonozuka Kofun]][[Category:前方後円墳]] [[Category:前方後円墳]][[sn:Nishitonozuka Kofun]][[Category:前方後円墳]] [[Category:前方後円墳]][[sn:Nishitonozuka Kofun]][[Category:前方後円墳]] [[Category:前方後円墳]][[sn:Nishitonozuka Kofun]][[Category:前方後円墳]]

revision.text:
{{Infobox ancient site |name = Nishitonozuka Kofun |image = [[File:Nishitonotsuka Kofun, zenkei.jpg|280px]]
Full view of the mound (front section on the right, rear circle in the back left) |Group = {{ill|Yamato Kofun Group|ja|大和古墳群|1=Ōyamato Kofun Group}} (Nakayama subgroup) |location = {{ill|Tenri, Nara Prefecture|ja|天理市}}, Nakayama Town, Nishitonozuka{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳（古墳）|1989}} |LatitudeDegrees = 34|LatitudeMinutes = 34|LatitudeSeconds = 6.22 |LongitudeDegrees = 135|LongitudeMinutes = 51|LongitudeSeconds = 4.26 |ISO = JP-29 |Type = {{ill|Keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳}} |Scale = Mound length approximately 230{{ill|Meters|ja|メートル}}
Height approximately 16m (rear circle) |Construction = Late {{ill|3rd century|ja|3世紀}} to its end |BurialFacility = Unknown |Interred = ({{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} designation) {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|ja|手白香皇女}}
(One theory) {{ill|Queen Himiko|ja|台与}}
(Another theory) Emperor {{ill|Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}} |Artifacts = {{ill|Special pedestal and pottery|ja|特殊器台・特殊壺}}, Miyama-style special pedestals and pottery
Ordinary cylindrical haniwa |Mausoleum = {{ill|Fusumada Mausoleum|ja|衾田陵}} (designated by the Imperial Household Agency) |Notes = Ranked 24th nationwide by size
(if mound length is considered 219m)[https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/ranking/zenkoku.html Ranking of Tumulus Sizes in Japan] (Sakai City website, updated May 13, 2018).
Considered the royal tomb following {{ill|Hashihaka Kofun|ja|箸墓古墳}} |Map = Japan Nara |Label = Nishitonozuka Kofun |LabelPosition = Top |Icon = Keyhole-shaped tomb - South }} [[File:Nishitonotsuka Kofun, haisho.jpg|thumb|220px|{{center|{{ill|Princess Tashiraka|ja|手白香皇女}} Fusumada Mausoleum Worship Site}}]] '''Nishitonozuka Kofun''' (西殿塚古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in {{ill|Tenri, Nara Prefecture|ja|天理市}}, Nakayama Town. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳}} and part of the {{ill|Yamato Kofun Group|ja|大和古墳群|1=Ōyamato Kofun Group}} (Nakayama subgroup). The identity of the interred is uncertain, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} designates the site as the '''Fusumada Mausoleum''' (衾田陵), the resting place of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|ja|手白香皇女}}, the consort of [[Emperor Keitai]] It is estimated to have been built in the latter half of the {{ill|3rd century|ja|3世紀}} (early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}) and is considered the royal tomb succeeding the earliest keyhole-shaped tomb, the {{ill|Hashihaka Kofun|ja|箸墓古墳}}. == Overview == It is a gigantic keyhole-shaped tumulus constructed on the hilly area along the eastern edge of the {{ill|Nara Basin|ja|奈良盆地}}. Adjacent to its eastern side is the {{ill|Higashitonotsuka Kofun|ja|東殿塚古墳|1=Higashitonotsuka Kofun}}, and these two, being at the highest point within the {{ill|Yamato Kofun Group|ja|大和古墳群|1=Ōyamato Kofun Group}}, offer a panoramic view of the entire basinHistoric Site Explanation Board.{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 陵墓篇 第65号|2014|pp=108-112}}. The tumulus has remained well preserved to the present day{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991|pp=100-111}}. It is currently managed by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as the mausoleum of an empress under its jurisdiction; to date, exterior investigations of the tumulus have been conducted by the {{ill|Archives and Mausolea Department|ja|宮内庁書陵部}} during the {{ill|1989|ja|1989年}} ({{ill|Heisei|ja|平成}} first fiscal year) period{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991|pp=100-111}}, surveys of the surrounding area by the Tenri City Board of Education during the {{ill|1992|ja|1992年|lt=1992|lt_ja=1992年}}–{{ill|1994|ja|1994年}} period (Heisei 4–6 fiscal years){{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=1-4}}, and an academic on-site survey in the {{ill|2012|ja|2012年}} period (Heisei 24 fiscal year){{R|2013年調査}}. The tumulus is of a keyhole shape with its anterior portion facing south; however, because it was constructed at a right angle to a sloping terrain (with the higher elevation on the east side), it takes on an asymmetrical form{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}. In the posterior circular portion, it is built with three tiers on the east side and four tiers on the west side, while in the anterior portion it is built with one tier on the east side and two tiers on the west side{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=5-7}}. The overall length of the tumulus measures about 230 {{ill|meters|ja|メートル}}, making it the largest within the Yamato Kofun Group. On its exterior, in addition to the presence of {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}}, early haniwa have been detected around the tumulus, including {{ill|Special platforms and jars|ja|特殊器台・特殊壺|lt=Special Kiderai-type earthenware, special Kiderai-type haniwa, special tsubo-shaped haniwa|lt_ja=特殊器台形土器・特殊器台形埴輪・特殊壺形埴輪}} (from the tumulus itself) and {{ill|Cylindrical Haniwa|ja|円筒埴輪|lt=cylindrical haniwa}} with a stepped neck{{R|説明板}}. Although the burial facilities remain unclear, square platforms (mounds) are present on both the posterior and anterior portions of the tumulus{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=5-7}}. This Nishitonozuka Kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the latter half of the {{ill|3rd century|ja|3世紀}} during the early part of the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}{{R|説明板}}[http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/miryoku/tenrinomiryoku1/kofun/1445323092951.html]{{ill|Nishitonozuka Kofun|ja|西殿塚古墳}} (Tenri City Homepage). It is regarded as the great tomb of the Yamato Kingdom that succeeded the {{ill|Hashihaka Kofun|ja|箸墓古墳}} (located in {{ill|Sakurai City|ja|桜井市}} Hashinaka){{R|白石}}, and in conjunction with the adjacent {{ill|Higaida-ōtsuka Kofun|ja|東殿塚古墳|1=Higashitonotsuka Kofun}}, it is considered to be part of a continuous construction sequence beginning with Nishitonozuka Kofun{{R|説明板}}. Although the identity of the interred remains unclear, it is currently designated by the Imperial Household Agency as the mausoleum of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|lt=Tebarakakōjo|ja|手白香皇女}} (the {{ill|Empress|ja|皇后}} of the 26th {{ill|Emperor Keitai|ja|継体天皇}} ){{Sfn|衾田陵（国史）}}. However, since the construction date does not correspond with the assumed period of the {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} for {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|lt=Tebarakakōjo|ja|手白香皇女}}, a theory that the true mausoleum of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|lt=Tebarakakōjo|ja|手白香皇女}} is the {{ill|Nishiyamazuka Kofun|ja|西山塚古墳}} (in Tenri City, Kayashō Town) is strongly supported{{Sfn|天理の古墳100|2015|p=55}}, while alternative theories propose that the true interred of this tumulus is {{ill|Toyo (queen)|ja|台与|lt=Queen Toyo}}, a successor to {{ill|Himiko|ja|卑弥呼}} (who may have been enshrined in the Hashihaka Kofun){{R|白石}}. [[category:New pages]][[ja:西殿塚古墳]] == Burial == The interred individual is not definitively known, but the site is officially designated as the resting place of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|ja|手白香皇女}}. However, the construction date (3rd century) conflicts with Princess Tashiraka’s presumed era (6th century), leading some to propose the nearby {{ill|Nishiyamazuka Kofun|ja|西山塚古墳}} as her true mausoleum.{{Sfn|天理の古墳100|2015|p=55}} Other theories suggest Queen {{ill|Himiko|ja|卑弥呼}}’s successor, {{ill|Toyo (queen)|ja|台与|lt=Queen Toyo}}, or [[Emperor Sujin]] as the interred individual.{{Sfn|白石太一郎|2013|pp=171-174}} == Site History == * {{ill|1876|ja|1876年}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治}} 9), designated as the mausoleum of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|lt=Tebarakakōjo|ja|手白香皇女}}{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 陵墓篇 第65号|2014|pp=108-112}}. * {{ill|1889|ja|1889年}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治}} 22), repaired and maintained as a mausoleum {{ill|Kinuta Tomb|ja|衾田陵（国史）}}. * {{ill|1986|ja|1986年}} period ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和}} 61 fiscal year), the first survey was conducted{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=1-4}}. * {{ill|1989|ja|1989年}} period ({{ill|Heisei|ja|平成}} first fiscal year), an exterior survey of the tumulus was carried out by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency Shoryo Department|ja|宮内庁書陵部}} {{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991|pp=100-111}}. * From {{ill|1992|ja|1992年|lt=1992|lt_ja=1992}} to {{ill|1994|ja|1994年}}, ({{ill|Heisei|ja|平成}} 4–6 fiscal years), the 2nd to 4th surveys were conducted by the Tenri City Board of Education{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=1-4}}. * {{ill|2012|ja|2012年}} ({{ill|Heisei|ja|平成}} 24): ** On April 9, an aerial 3D survey was conducted by the {{ill|Nara Prefectural Kashihara Archaeological Institute|ja|奈良県立橿原考古学研究所}} and {{ill|Asia Aerial Surveying|ja|アジア航測}}{{PDFlink|[http://www.ajiko.co.jp/news/2012/hashihaka_rittaichizu.pdf "Creation of a Red-colored 3D Map of the Hashihaka and Seidenzuka Kofun"]}} (Press release from the Nara Prefectural Kashihara Archaeological Institute and Asia Aerial Surveying Co., Ltd., 2012).[https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXNASDG0503K_V00C12A6CR8000/ "Himiko’s Tomb? 3D Helicopter Survey of the Hashihaka Kofun by Kashihara Institute, etc."] (Nikkei, June 5, 2012).. ** In August, following a theft incident (with no destruction of the remains) and subsequent restoration, a survey was carried out by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency Shoryo Department|ja|宮内庁書陵部}} {{Sfn|書陵部紀要 陵墓篇 第65号|2014|pp=108-112}}. * {{ill|2013|ja|2013年}} ({{ill|Heisei|ja|平成}} 25) on February 20, an on-site survey was conducted by representatives of 15 academic societies in archaeology and history[https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXNASDG1905C_Q3A220C1CR0000/ "Himiko’s Tomb? First On-site Survey at the Hashihaka Kofun in Nara, Raising Expectations for Research Progress"] (Nikkei, February 20, 2013).. == Tumulus == [[File:Tonotono-tsuka stereo.jpg|thumb|{{center|Nishitonozuka Kofun's {{ill|Stereogram|ja|ステレオグラム|lt=Stereogram|lt_ja=ステレオ}} Aerial Photograph (1979) In the image, the {{ill|Higashidenzuka Kofun|ja|東殿塚古墳|1=Higashitonotsuka Kofun}} is shown at the top and the {{ill|Seidenzuka Kofun|ja|西殿塚古墳|1=Nishitonozuka Kofun}} at the bottom. {{ill|National Aerial Photography|ja|国土航空写真}}.]] The dimensions of the tumulus are as follows{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=5-7}}. * Tumulus length: approximately 230 meters (in some sources, 234 meters{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}, 220 meters{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 陵墓篇 第65号|2014|pp=108-112}}, or 219 meters{{R|堺市}}). * Posterior circular portion – built with 3 tiers on the east side and 4 tiers on the west side. ** Diameter: approximately 140 meters ** Height: approximately 16 meters (east side) * Anterior portion – built with 1 tier on the east side and 2 tiers on the west side. ** Width: approximately 130 meters ** Height: approximately 12 meters (east side) * Square platform (mound) – built in one tier. ** Posterior circular portion: 25.15 meters east–west, 26.54 meters north–south, height 3.00 meters{{R|2012年報道発表資料}} ** Anterior portion: 12.92 meters east–west, 14.43 meters north–south, height 1.87 meters{{R|2012年報道発表資料}} In the theory where the tumulus length is taken as 219 meters, it ranks as the 24th largest in the country{{R|堺市}}. The tiered terraces of the tumulus do not directly connect the posterior circular and anterior portions; the difference in tiers between these portions is reconciled in the constricted section{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991|pp=100-111}}. Furthermore, on the western side of the tumulus, a broad, flat surface (apron), characteristic of the Nishitonozuka Kofun, has been shaped as the lowest tier{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=5-7}}. On the eastern side of the tumulus, there are two bridge-like structures located in the central area of the posterior circular portion and on the southern side of the anterior portion, both of which connect to the adjacent {{ill|Higashidenzuka Kofun|ja|東殿塚古墳|1=Higashitonotsuka Kofun}}{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=5-7}}. == Interred ==
'''Family Tree Based on the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}}'''The reign information is based on the {{ill|Nihon Jinmei Daijiten|ja|日本人名大辞典}} (Kodansha). {{familytree/start|style="text-align:left; font-size:100%"}} {{familytree|border=0|||||01| 01={{sup|24}} {{ill|Emperor Ninken|ja|仁賢天皇}}
{{small|(Reign: end of 5th century)}}}} {{familytree|border=0|||||||)|.}} {{familytree|border=0|01|y|02|03| 01={{sup|26}} {{ill|Emperor Keitai|ja|継体天皇}}
{{small|(Reign: 507?-531?)}}|02={{ill|Princess Tashiraka|lt=Tebarakakōjo|ja|手白香皇女}}|03={{sup|25}} {{ill|Emperor Buretsu|ja|武烈天皇}}
{{small|(Reign: end of 5th century – early 6th century)}}}} {{familytree|border=0||||01|| 01={{sup|29}} {{ill|Emperor Kinmei|ja|欽明天皇}}
{{small|(Reign: 539?-571?)}}}} {{familytree/end}}
The actual interred of the {{ill|Seidenzuka Kofun|ja|西殿塚古墳|1=Nishitonozuka Kofun}} remains unclear; however, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} designates it as the mausoleum of the 26th {{ill|Emperor Keitai|ja|継体天皇}}’s consort, '''{{ill|Princess Tashiraka|lt=Tebarakakōjo|ja|手白香皇女}}''' (Tashiraka no Hime-miko, also rendered as Tashiraka no Hairarō/ Tashiraka no Himemi){{Sfn|衾田陵（国史）}}Compiled by the Imperial Ministry of Mausolea [{{NDLDC|1237123/11}} "Guide to Mausolea"] (1934, National Diet Library Digital Collection), 11 panels."Compilation of Mausoleum Topographical Maps, Abbreviated Edition", compiled by the Imperial Household Agency Shoryo Department Mausoleum Section, [[Gakuseisha]], 2014, p. 406.. Although the mausoleum of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|lt=Tebarakakōjo|ja|手白香皇女}} is not mentioned in either the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} or the {{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}}, in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}’s mausolea section (displayed as {{ill|Shoryo Department|ja|諸陵寮}}) it is recorded as the distant "Kinuta Tomb". It is said to be located in {{ill|Yamato Province|ja|大和国}}’s {{ill|Yamabe District|ja|山辺郡}}, covering an area of two chō east–west and two chō north–south, with no separate guard door, the mound door of the Kamikami Burial Mound of Yamabe (the mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Sushin|ja|崇神天皇}}) concurrently serving as its guard{{Sfn|衾田陵（国史）}}. Later, during the {{ill|Medieval period|ja|中世}}, the traditional accounts regarding the location of the mausoleum were lost{{Sfn|衾田陵（国史）}}. In {{ill|1876|ja|1876年}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治}} 9), the {{ill|Kyōbushō|ja|教部省}} designated the {{ill|Seidenzuka Kofun|ja|西殿塚古墳|1=Nishitonozuka Kofun}} as the mausoleum, and in {{ill|1889|ja|1889年}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治}} 22) repairs were carried out{{Sfn|衾田陵（国史）}}. [[File:Hashihaka-kofun zenkei.JPG|サムネイル|220px|{{center|{{ill|Hashihaka Kofun|ja|箸墓古墳}} (located in {{ill|Sakurai City|ja|桜井市}}, Hashinaka)}}{{small|Attributed to {{ill|Wajishiki no Hime|ja|倭迹迹日百襲姫命}}. Archaeologically, it is considered either the tomb of the first great king of the {{ill|Yamato Kingdom|ja|ヤマト王権}} or the tomb of {{ill|Himiko|ja|卑弥呼}}.}}]] On the other hand, regarding the true mausoleum of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|lt=Tebarakakōjo|ja|手白香皇女}}, a prevailing theory holds that it should be identified not with the Nishitonozuka Kofun but with the {{ill|Nishiyamazuka Kofun|ja|西山塚古墳}} (located in Tenri City, Kayashō Town){{Sfn|天理の古墳100|2015|p=55}}. This theory is based on the fact that while the construction date of the Nishitonozuka Kofun is estimated to be around the latter half of the 3rd century, the date for the Nishiyamazuka Kofun is around the {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}}, which corresponds with the assumed period for {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|lt=Tebarakakōjo|ja|手白香皇女}}{{Sfn|天理の古墳100|2015|p=55}}. Meanwhile, as for the true interred of the Nishitonozuka Kofun, some theories propose that it is {{ill|Daiyo|ja|台与}} (also written 壹與/臺與), based on its subsequent position to the {{ill|Hashihaka Kofun|ja|箸墓古墳}}—regarded as the tomb of {{ill|Himiko|ja|卑弥呼}}—or that it is {{ill|Emperor Sushin|ja|崇神天皇}}{{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, ''The Formation and Development of the Wa Kingdom as Seen from the Kofun'', Keibunsha, 2013, pp. 171-174.,{{ill|Suiz Wada|ja|和田萃}} “On the Yamabe Road”, in ''The Ancient History of Mount Miwa'', Gakuseisha, 2003. among others. {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%" |+ Estimated Early Great King Tombs of the Yamato Kingdom
{{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, ''The Formation and Development of the Wa Kingdom as Seen from the Kofun'' (日本歴史 私の最新講義), Keibunsha, 2013, pp. 181-186. ! Order !! Tumulus Name |- |1||{{ill|Hashihaka Kofun|ja|箸墓古墳}} |- |2||'''{{ill|Nishitonozuka Kofun|ja|西殿塚古墳|1=Nishitonozuka Kofun}}''' |- |3||{{ill|Sakurai Chausuyama Kofun|ja|桜井茶臼山古墳|lt=Sakurai Chausuyama Kofun|lt_ja=外山茶臼山古墳}} |- |4||{{ill|Mesuriyama Kofun|ja|メスリ山古墳}} |- |5||{{ill|Andonyama Kofun|ja|行燈山古墳}} |- |6||{{ill|Shibuya Mukaeyama Kofun|ja|渋谷向山古墳}} |} == References == {{Reflist|2}} == Further Reading == * Site explanation board, Tenri City Board of Education, 2010. * {{Cite book|和書|title=Nishitonozuka Kofun and Higashitonozuka Kofun (Tenri City Cultural Heritage Report No.7)|publisher=Tenri City Board of Education|year=2000|ref={{Harvid|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|title=100 Kofun in Tenri|publisher=Tenri City Board of Education|year=2015|ref={{Harvid|天理の古墳100|2015}}}} == Related Articles == * {{ill|Yamato Kofun Group|ja|大和古墳群|1=Ōyamato Kofun Group}} * {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|ja|手白香皇女}} == External Links == * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/miryoku/tenrinomiryoku1/kofun/1445323092951.html Nishitonozuka Kofun - Tenri City website] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Yamato Kofun Group]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Nara Prefecture]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:History of Tenri]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Imperial Tombs of Japan]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]] [[Category:kk]] [[Category:Fixed Kofun templates]] {{Kofun navbar}} [[Category:Fixed Kofun templates]] [[Category:kk]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:Nishitonozuka Kofun]][[Category:kk]] [[Category:qq]][[Category:Nishitonozuka Kofun]][[Category:qq]] [[ja:西殿塚古墳]] [[Category:new pages]] [[Category:大和古墳群]] [[Category:前方後円墳]][[sn:Nishitonozuka Kofun]][[Category:前方後円墳]] [[Category:前方後円墳]][[sn:Nishitonozuka Kofun]][[Category:前方後円墳]] [[Category:前方後円墳]][[sn:Nishitonozuka Kofun]][[Category:前方後円墳]] [[Category:前方後円墳]][[sn:Nishitonozuka Kofun]][[Category:前方後円墳]] [[Category:前方後円墳]][[sn:Nishitonozuka Kofun]][[Category:前方後円墳]]

revision.text:
{{Infobox ancient site |name = Nishitonozuka Kofun |image = [[File:Nishitonotsuka Kofun, zenkei.jpg|280px]]
Full view of the mound (front section on the right, rear circle in the back left) |Group = {{ill|Yamato Kofun Group|ja|大和古墳群|1=Ōyamato Kofun Group}} (Nakayama subgroup) |location = {{ill|Tenri, Nara Prefecture|ja|天理市}}, Nakayama Town, Nishitonozuka{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳（古墳）|1989}} |LatitudeDegrees = 34|LatitudeMinutes = 34|LatitudeSeconds = 6.22 |LongitudeDegrees = 135|LongitudeMinutes = 51|LongitudeSeconds = 4.26 |ISO = JP-29 |Type = {{ill|Keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳}} |Scale = Mound length approximately 230{{ill|Meters|ja|メートル}}
Height approximately 16m (rear circle) |Construction = Late {{ill|3rd century|ja|3世紀}} to its end |BurialFacility = Unknown |Interred = ({{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} designation) {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|ja|手白香皇女}}
(One theory) {{ill|Queen Himiko|ja|台与}}
(Another theory) Emperor {{ill|Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}} |Artifacts = {{ill|Special pedestal and pottery|ja|特殊器台・特殊壺}}, Miyama-style special pedestals and pottery
Ordinary cylindrical haniwa |Mausoleum = {{ill|Fusumada Mausoleum|ja|衾田陵}} (designated by the Imperial Household Agency) |Notes = Ranked 24th nationwide by size
(if mound length is considered 219m)[https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/ranking/zenkoku.html Ranking of Tumulus Sizes in Japan] (Sakai City website, updated May 13, 2018).
Considered the royal tomb following {{ill|Hashihaka Kofun|ja|箸墓古墳}} |Map = Japan Nara |Label = Nishitonozuka Kofun |LabelPosition = Top |Icon = Keyhole-shaped tomb - South }} [[File:Nishitonotsuka Kofun, haisho.jpg|thumb|220px|{{center|{{ill|Princess Tashiraka|ja|手白香皇女}} Fusumada Mausoleum Worship Site}}]] '''Nishitonozuka Kofun''' (西殿塚古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in {{ill|Tenri, Nara Prefecture|ja|天理市}}, Nakayama Town. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳}} and part of the {{ill|Yamato Kofun Group|ja|大和古墳群|1=Ōyamato Kofun Group}} (Nakayama subgroup). The identity of the interred is uncertain, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} designates the site as the '''Fusumada Mausoleum''' (衾田陵), the resting place of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|ja|手白香皇女}}, the consort of [[Emperor Keitai]] It is estimated to have been built in the latter half of the {{ill|3rd century|ja|3世紀}} (early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}) and is considered the royal tomb succeeding the earliest keyhole-shaped tomb, the {{ill|Hashihaka Kofun|ja|箸墓古墳}}. == Overview == It is a gigantic keyhole-shaped tumulus constructed on the hilly area along the eastern edge of the {{ill|Nara Basin|ja|奈良盆地}}. Adjacent to its eastern side is the {{ill|Higashitonotsuka Kofun|ja|東殿塚古墳|1=Higashitonotsuka Kofun}}, and these two, being at the highest point within the {{ill|Yamato Kofun Group|ja|大和古墳群|1=Ōyamato Kofun Group}}, offer a panoramic view of the entire basinHistoric Site Explanation Board.{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 陵墓篇 第65号|2014|pp=108-112}}. The tumulus has remained well preserved to the present day{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991|pp=100-111}}. It is currently managed by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as the mausoleum of an empress under its jurisdiction; to date, exterior investigations of the tumulus have been conducted by the {{ill|Archives and Mausolea Department|ja|宮内庁書陵部}} during the {{ill|1989|ja|1989年}} ({{ill|Heisei|ja|平成}} first fiscal year) period{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991|pp=100-111}}, surveys of the surrounding area by the Tenri City Board of Education during the {{ill|1992|ja|1992年|lt=1992|lt_ja=1992年}}–{{ill|1994|ja|1994年}} period (Heisei 4–6 fiscal years){{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=1-4}}, and an academic on-site survey in the {{ill|2012|ja|2012年}} period (Heisei 24 fiscal year){{R|2013年調査}}. The tumulus is of a keyhole shape with its anterior portion facing south; however, because it was constructed at a right angle to a sloping terrain (with the higher elevation on the east side), it takes on an asymmetrical form{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}. In the posterior circular portion, it is built with three tiers on the east side and four tiers on the west side, while in the anterior portion it is built with one tier on the east side and two tiers on the west side{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=5-7}}. The overall length of the tumulus measures about 230 {{ill|meters|ja|メートル}}, making it the largest within the Yamato Kofun Group. On its exterior, in addition to the presence of {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}}, early haniwa have been detected around the tumulus, including {{ill|Special platforms and jars|ja|特殊器台・特殊壺|lt=Special Kiderai-type earthenware, special Kiderai-type haniwa, special tsubo-shaped haniwa|lt_ja=特殊器台形土器・特殊器台形埴輪・特殊壺形埴輪}} (from the tumulus itself) and {{ill|Cylindrical Haniwa|ja|円筒埴輪|lt=cylindrical haniwa}} with a stepped neck{{R|説明板}}. Although the burial facilities remain unclear, square platforms (mounds) are present on both the posterior and anterior portions of the tumulus{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=5-7}}. This Nishitonozuka Kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the latter half of the {{ill|3rd century|ja|3世紀}} during the early part of the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}{{R|説明板}}[http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/miryoku/tenrinomiryoku1/kofun/1445323092951.html]{{ill|Nishitonozuka Kofun|ja|西殿塚古墳}} (Tenri City Homepage). It is regarded as the great tomb of the Yamato Kingdom that succeeded the {{ill|Hashihaka Kofun|ja|箸墓古墳}} (located in {{ill|Sakurai City|ja|桜井市}} Hashinaka){{R|白石}}, and in conjunction with the adjacent {{ill|Higaida-ōtsuka Kofun|ja|東殿塚古墳|1=Higashitonotsuka Kofun}}, it is considered to be part of a continuous construction sequence beginning with Nishitonozuka Kofun{{R|説明板}}. Although the identity of the interred remains unclear, it is currently designated by the Imperial Household Agency as the mausoleum of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|lt=Tebarakakōjo|ja|手白香皇女}} (the {{ill|Empress|ja|皇后}} of the 26th {{ill|Emperor Keitai|ja|継体天皇}} ){{Sfn|衾田陵（国史）}}. However, since the construction date does not correspond with the assumed period of the {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} for {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|lt=Tebarakakōjo|ja|手白香皇女}}, a theory that the true mausoleum of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|lt=Tebarakakōjo|ja|手白香皇女}} is the {{ill|Nishiyamazuka Kofun|ja|西山塚古墳}} (in Tenri City, Kayashō Town) is strongly supported{{Sfn|天理の古墳100|2015|p=55}}, while alternative theories propose that the true interred of this tumulus is {{ill|Toyo (queen)|ja|台与|lt=Queen Toyo}}, a successor to {{ill|Himiko|ja|卑弥呼}} (who may have been enshrined in the Hashihaka Kofun){{R|白石}}. [[category:New pages]][[ja:西殿塚古墳]] == Burial == The interred individual is not definitively known, but the site is officially designated as the resting place of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|ja|手白香皇女}}. However, the construction date (3rd century) conflicts with Princess Tashiraka’s presumed era (6th century), leading some to propose the nearby {{ill|Nishiyamazuka Kofun|ja|西山塚古墳}} as her true mausoleum.{{Sfn|天理の古墳100|2015|p=55}} Other theories suggest Queen {{ill|Himiko|ja|卑弥呼}}’s successor, {{ill|Toyo (queen)|ja|台与|lt=Queen Toyo}}, or [[Emperor Sujin]] as the interred individual.{{Sfn|白石太一郎|2013|pp=171-174}} == Site History == * {{ill|1876|ja|1876年}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治}} 9), designated as the mausoleum of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|lt=Tebarakakōjo|ja|手白香皇女}}{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 陵墓篇 第65号|2014|pp=108-112}}. * {{ill|1889|ja|1889年}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治}} 22), repaired and maintained as a mausoleum {{ill|Kinuta Tomb|ja|衾田陵（国史）}}. * {{ill|1986|ja|1986年}} period ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和}} 61 fiscal year), the first survey was conducted{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=1-4}}. * {{ill|1989|ja|1989年}} period ({{ill|Heisei|ja|平成}} first fiscal year), an exterior survey of the tumulus was carried out by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency Shoryo Department|ja|宮内庁書陵部}} {{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991|pp=100-111}}. * From {{ill|1992|ja|1992年|lt=1992|lt_ja=1992}} to {{ill|1994|ja|1994年}}, ({{ill|Heisei|ja|平成}} 4–6 fiscal years), the 2nd to 4th surveys were conducted by the Tenri City Board of Education{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=1-4}}. * {{ill|2012|ja|2012年}} ({{ill|Heisei|ja|平成}} 24): ** On April 9, an aerial 3D survey was conducted by the {{ill|Nara Prefectural Kashihara Archaeological Institute|ja|奈良県立橿原考古学研究所}} and {{ill|Asia Aerial Surveying|ja|アジア航測}}{{PDFlink|[http://www.ajiko.co.jp/news/2012/hashihaka_rittaichizu.pdf "Creation of a Red-colored 3D Map of the Hashihaka and Seidenzuka Kofun"]}} (Press release from the Nara Prefectural Kashihara Archaeological Institute and Asia Aerial Surveying Co., Ltd., 2012).[https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXNASDG0503K_V00C12A6CR8000/ "Himiko’s Tomb? 3D Helicopter Survey of the Hashihaka Kofun by Kashihara Institute, etc."] (Nikkei, June 5, 2012).. ** In August, following a theft incident (with no destruction of the remains) and subsequent restoration, a survey was carried out by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency Shoryo Department|ja|宮内庁書陵部}} {{Sfn|書陵部紀要 陵墓篇 第65号|2014|pp=108-112}}. * {{ill|2013|ja|2013年}} ({{ill|Heisei|ja|平成}} 25) on February 20, an on-site survey was conducted by representatives of 15 academic societies in archaeology and history[https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXNASDG1905C_Q3A220C1CR0000/ "Himiko’s Tomb? First On-site Survey at the Hashihaka Kofun in Nara, Raising Expectations for Research Progress"] (Nikkei, February 20, 2013).. == Tumulus == [[File:Tonotono-tsuka stereo.jpg|thumb|{{center|Nishitonozuka Kofun's {{ill|Stereogram|ja|ステレオグラム|lt=Stereogram|lt_ja=ステレオ}} Aerial Photograph (1979) In the image, the {{ill|Higashidenzuka Kofun|ja|東殿塚古墳|1=Higashitonotsuka Kofun}} is shown at the top and the {{ill|Seidenzuka Kofun|ja|西殿塚古墳|1=Nishitonozuka Kofun}} at the bottom. {{ill|National Aerial Photography|ja|国土航空写真}}.]] The dimensions of the tumulus are as follows{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=5-7}}. * Tumulus length: approximately 230 meters (in some sources, 234 meters{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}, 220 meters{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 陵墓篇 第65号|2014|pp=108-112}}, or 219 meters{{R|堺市}}). * Posterior circular portion – built with 3 tiers on the east side and 4 tiers on the west side. ** Diameter: approximately 140 meters ** Height: approximately 16 meters (east side) * Anterior portion – built with 1 tier on the east side and 2 tiers on the west side. ** Width: approximately 130 meters ** Height: approximately 12 meters (east side) * Square platform (mound) – built in one tier. ** Posterior circular portion: 25.15 meters east–west, 26.54 meters north–south, height 3.00 meters{{R|2012年報道発表資料}} ** Anterior portion: 12.92 meters east–west, 14.43 meters north–south, height 1.87 meters{{R|2012年報道発表資料}} In the theory where the tumulus length is taken as 219 meters, it ranks as the 24th largest in the country{{R|堺市}}. The tiered terraces of the tumulus do not directly connect the posterior circular and anterior portions; the difference in tiers between these portions is reconciled in the constricted section{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991|pp=100-111}}. Furthermore, on the western side of the tumulus, a broad, flat surface (apron), characteristic of the Nishitonozuka Kofun, has been shaped as the lowest tier{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=5-7}}. On the eastern side of the tumulus, there are two bridge-like structures located in the central area of the posterior circular portion and on the southern side of the anterior portion, both of which connect to the adjacent {{ill|Higashidenzuka Kofun|ja|東殿塚古墳|1=Higashitonotsuka Kofun}}{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=5-7}}. == Interred ==
'''Family Tree Based on the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}}'''The reign information is based on the {{ill|Nihon Jinmei Daijiten|ja|日本人名大辞典}} (Kodansha). {{familytree/start|style="text-align:left; font-size:100%"}} {{familytree|border=0|||||01| 01={{sup|24}} {{ill|Emperor Ninken|ja|仁賢天皇}}
{{small|(Reign: end of 5th century)}}}} {{familytree|border=0|||||||)|.}} {{familytree|border=0|01|y|02|03| 01={{sup|26}} {{ill|Emperor Keitai|ja|継体天皇}}
{{small|(Reign: 507?-531?)}}|02={{ill|Princess Tashiraka|lt=Tebarakakōjo|ja|手白香皇女}}|03={{sup|25}} {{ill|Emperor Buretsu|ja|武烈天皇}}
{{small|(Reign: end of 5th century – early 6th century)}}}} {{familytree|border=0||||01|| 01={{sup|29}} {{ill|Emperor Kinmei|ja|欽明天皇}}
{{small|(Reign: 539?-571?)}}}} {{familytree/end}}
The actual interred of the {{ill|Seidenzuka Kofun|ja|西殿塚古墳|1=Nishitonozuka Kofun}} remains unclear; however, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} designates it as the mausoleum of the 26th {{ill|Emperor Keitai|ja|継体天皇}}’s consort, '''{{ill|Princess Tashiraka|lt=Tebarakakōjo|ja|手白香皇女}}''' (Tashiraka no Hime-miko, also rendered as Tashiraka no Hairarō/ Tashiraka no Himemi){{Sfn|衾田陵（国史）}}Compiled by the Imperial Ministry of Mausolea [{{NDLDC|1237123/11}} "Guide to Mausolea"] (1934, National Diet Library Digital Collection), 11 panels."Compilation of Mausoleum Topographical Maps, Abbreviated Edition", compiled by the Imperial Household Agency Shoryo Department Mausoleum Section, [[Gakuseisha]], 2014, p. 406.. Although the mausoleum of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|lt=Tebarakakōjo|ja|手白香皇女}} is not mentioned in either the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} or the {{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}}, in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}’s mausolea section (displayed as {{ill|Shoryo Department|ja|諸陵寮}}) it is recorded as the distant "Kinuta Tomb". It is said to be located in {{ill|Yamato Province|ja|大和国}}’s {{ill|Yamabe District|ja|山辺郡}}, covering an area of two chō east–west and two chō north–south, with no separate guard door, the mound door of the Kamikami Burial Mound of Yamabe (the mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Sushin|ja|崇神天皇}}) concurrently serving as its guard{{Sfn|衾田陵（国史）}}. Later, during the {{ill|Medieval period|ja|中世}}, the traditional accounts regarding the location of the mausoleum were lost{{Sfn|衾田陵（国史）}}. In {{ill|1876|ja|1876年}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治}} 9), the {{ill|Kyōbushō|ja|教部省}} designated the {{ill|Seidenzuka Kofun|ja|西殿塚古墳|1=Nishitonozuka Kofun}} as the mausoleum, and in {{ill|1889|ja|1889年}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治}} 22) repairs were carried out{{Sfn|衾田陵（国史）}}. [[File:Hashihaka-kofun zenkei.JPG|サムネイル|220px|{{center|{{ill|Hashihaka Kofun|ja|箸墓古墳}} (located in {{ill|Sakurai City|ja|桜井市}}, Hashinaka)}}{{small|Attributed to {{ill|Wajishiki no Hime|ja|倭迹迹日百襲姫命}}. Archaeologically, it is considered either the tomb of the first great king of the {{ill|Yamato Kingdom|ja|ヤマト王権}} or the tomb of {{ill|Himiko|ja|卑弥呼}}.}}]] On the other hand, regarding the true mausoleum of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|lt=Tebarakakōjo|ja|手白香皇女}}, a prevailing theory holds that it should be identified not with the Nishitonozuka Kofun but with the {{ill|Nishiyamazuka Kofun|ja|西山塚古墳}} (located in Tenri City, Kayashō Town){{Sfn|天理の古墳100|2015|p=55}}. This theory is based on the fact that while the construction date of the Nishitonozuka Kofun is estimated to be around the latter half of the 3rd century, the date for the Nishiyamazuka Kofun is around the {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}}, which corresponds with the assumed period for {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|lt=Tebarakakōjo|ja|手白香皇女}}{{Sfn|天理の古墳100|2015|p=55}}. Meanwhile, as for the true interred of the Nishitonozuka Kofun, some theories propose that it is {{ill|Daiyo|ja|台与}} (also written 壹與/臺與), based on its subsequent position to the {{ill|Hashihaka Kofun|ja|箸墓古墳}}—regarded as the tomb of {{ill|Himiko|ja|卑弥呼}}—or that it is {{ill|Emperor Sushin|ja|崇神天皇}}{{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, ''The Formation and Development of the Wa Kingdom as Seen from the Kofun'', Keibunsha, 2013, pp. 171-174.,{{ill|Suiz Wada|ja|和田萃}} “On the Yamabe Road”, in ''The Ancient History of Mount Miwa'', Gakuseisha, 2003. among others. {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%" |+ Estimated Early Great King Tombs of the Yamato Kingdom
{{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, ''The Formation and Development of the Wa Kingdom as Seen from the Kofun'' (日本歴史 私の最新講義), Keibunsha, 2013, pp. 181-186. ! Order !! Tumulus Name |- |1||{{ill|Hashihaka Kofun|ja|箸墓古墳}} |- |2||'''{{ill|Nishitonozuka Kofun|ja|西殿塚古墳|1=Nishitonozuka Kofun}}''' |- |3||{{ill|Sakurai Chausuyama Kofun|ja|桜井茶臼山古墳|lt=Sakurai Chausuyama Kofun|lt_ja=外山茶臼山古墳}} |- |4||{{ill|Mesuriyama Kofun|ja|メスリ山古墳}} |- |5||{{ill|Andonyama Kofun|ja|行燈山古墳}} |- |6||{{ill|Shibuya Mukaeyama Kofun|ja|渋谷向山古墳}} |} == References == {{Reflist|2}} == Further Reading == * Site explanation board, Tenri City Board of Education, 2010. * {{Cite book|和書|title=Nishitonozuka Kofun and Higashitonozuka Kofun (Tenri City Cultural Heritage Report No.7)|publisher=Tenri City Board of Education|year=2000|ref={{Harvid|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|title=100 Kofun in Tenri|publisher=Tenri City Board of Education|year=2015|ref={{Harvid|天理の古墳100|2015}}}} == Related Articles == * {{ill|Yamato Kofun Group|ja|大和古墳群|1=Ōyamato Kofun Group}} * {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|ja|手白香皇女}} == External Links == * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/miryoku/tenrinomiryoku1/kofun/1445323092951.html Nishitonozuka Kofun - revision.text:
{{Infobox ancient site |name = Nishitonozuka Kofun |image = [[File:Nishitonotsuka Kofun, zenkei.jpg|280px]]
Full view of the mound (front section on the right, rear circle in the back left) |Group = {{ill|Yamato Kofun Group|ja|大和古墳群|1=Ōyamato Kofun Group}} (Nakayama subgroup) |location = {{ill|Tenri, Nara Prefecture|ja|天理市}}, Nakayama Town, Nishitonozuka{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳（古墳）|1989}} |LatitudeDegrees = 34|LatitudeMinutes = 34|LatitudeSeconds = 6.22 |LongitudeDegrees = 135|LongitudeMinutes = 51|LongitudeSeconds = 4.26 |ISO = JP-29 |Type = {{ill|Keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳}} |Scale = Mound length approximately 230{{ill|Meters|ja|メートル}}
Height approximately 16m (rear circle) |Construction = Late {{ill|3rd century|ja|3世紀}} to its end |BurialFacility = Unknown |Interred = ({{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} designation) {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|ja|手白香皇女}}
(One theory) {{ill|Queen Himiko|ja|台与}}
(Another theory) Emperor {{ill|Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}} |Artifacts = {{ill|Special pedestal and pottery|ja|特殊器台・特殊壺}}, Miyama-style special pedestals and pottery
Ordinary cylindrical haniwa |Mausoleum = {{ill|Fusumada Mausoleum|ja|衾田陵}} (designated by the Imperial Household Agency) |Notes = Ranked 24th nationwide by size
(if mound length is considered 219m)[https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/ranking/zenkoku.html Ranking of Tumulus Sizes in Japan] (Sakai City website, updated May 13, 2018).
Considered the royal tomb following {{ill|Hashihaka Kofun|ja|箸墓古墳}} |Map = Japan Nara |Label = Nishitonozuka Kofun |LabelPosition = Top |Icon = Keyhole-shaped tomb - South }} [[File:Nishitonotsuka Kofun, haisho.jpg|thumb|220px|{{center|{{ill|Princess Tashiraka|ja|手白香皇女}} Fusumada Mausoleum Worship Site}}]] '''Nishitonozuka Kofun''' (西殿塚古墳) is a {{ill|kofun|ja|古墳}} located in {{ill|Tenri, Nara Prefecture|ja|天理市}}, Nakayama Town. It is a {{ill|keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳}} and part of the {{ill|Yamato Kofun Group|ja|大和古墳群|1=Ōyamato Kofun Group}} (Nakayama subgroup). The identity of the interred is uncertain, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} designates the site as the '''Fusumada Mausoleum''' (衾田陵), the resting place of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|ja|手白香皇女}}, the consort of [[Emperor Keitai]] It is estimated to have been built in the latter half of the {{ill|3rd century|ja|3世紀}} (early {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}) and is considered the royal tomb succeeding the earliest keyhole-shaped tomb, the {{ill|Hashihaka Kofun|ja|箸墓古墳}}. == Overview == It is a gigantic keyhole-shaped tumulus constructed on the hilly area along the eastern edge of the {{ill|Nara Basin|ja|奈良盆地}}. Adjacent to its eastern side is the {{ill|Higashitonotsuka Kofun|ja|東殿塚古墳|1=Higashitonotsuka Kofun}}, and these two, being at the highest point within the {{ill|Yamato Kofun Group|ja|大和古墳群|1=Ōyamato Kofun Group}}, offer a panoramic view of the entire basinHistoric Site Explanation Board.{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 陵墓篇 第65号|2014|pp=108-112}}. The tumulus has remained well preserved to the present day{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991|pp=100-111}}. It is currently managed by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} as the mausoleum of an empress under its jurisdiction; to date, exterior investigations of the tumulus have been conducted by the {{ill|Archives and Mausolea Department|ja|宮内庁書陵部}} during the {{ill|1989|ja|1989年}} ({{ill|Heisei|ja|平成}} first fiscal year) period{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991|pp=100-111}}, surveys of the surrounding area by the Tenri City Board of Education during the {{ill|1992|ja|1992年|lt=1992|lt_ja=1992年}}–{{ill|1994|ja|1994年}} period (Heisei 4–6 fiscal years){{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=1-4}}, and an academic on-site survey in the {{ill|2012|ja|2012年}} period (Heisei 24 fiscal year){{R|2013年調査}}. The tumulus is of a keyhole shape with its anterior portion facing south; however, because it was constructed at a right angle to a sloping terrain (with the higher elevation on the east side), it takes on an asymmetrical form{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}. In the posterior circular portion, it is built with three tiers on the east side and four tiers on the west side, while in the anterior portion it is built with one tier on the east side and two tiers on the west side{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=5-7}}. The overall length of the tumulus measures about 230 {{ill|meters|ja|メートル}}, making it the largest within the Yamato Kofun Group. On its exterior, in addition to the presence of {{ill|Fukiishi|ja|葺石}}, early haniwa have been detected around the tumulus, including {{ill|Special platforms and jars|ja|特殊器台・特殊壺|lt=Special Kiderai-type earthenware, special Kiderai-type haniwa, special tsubo-shaped haniwa|lt_ja=特殊器台形土器・特殊器台形埴輪・特殊壺形埴輪}} (from the tumulus itself) and {{ill|Cylindrical Haniwa|ja|円筒埴輪|lt=cylindrical haniwa}} with a stepped neck{{R|説明板}}. Although the burial facilities remain unclear, square platforms (mounds) are present on both the posterior and anterior portions of the tumulus{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=5-7}}. This Nishitonozuka Kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the latter half of the {{ill|3rd century|ja|3世紀}} during the early part of the {{ill|Kofun period|ja|古墳時代}}{{R|説明板}}[http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/miryoku/tenrinomiryoku1/kofun/1445323092951.html]{{ill|Nishitonozuka Kofun|ja|西殿塚古墳}} (Tenri City Homepage). It is regarded as the great tomb of the Yamato Kingdom that succeeded the {{ill|Hashihaka Kofun|ja|箸墓古墳}} (located in {{ill|Sakurai City|ja|桜井市}} Hashinaka){{R|白石}}, and in conjunction with the adjacent {{ill|Higaida-ōtsuka Kofun|ja|東殿塚古墳|1=Higashitonotsuka Kofun}}, it is considered to be part of a continuous construction sequence beginning with Nishitonozuka Kofun{{R|説明板}}. Although the identity of the interred remains unclear, it is currently designated by the Imperial Household Agency as the mausoleum of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|lt=Tebarakakōjo|ja|手白香皇女}} (the {{ill|Empress|ja|皇后}} of the 26th {{ill|Emperor Keitai|ja|継体天皇}} ){{Sfn|衾田陵（国史）}}. However, since the construction date does not correspond with the assumed period of the {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}} for {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|lt=Tebarakakōjo|ja|手白香皇女}}, a theory that the true mausoleum of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|lt=Tebarakakōjo|ja|手白香皇女}} is the {{ill|Nishiyamazuka Kofun|ja|西山塚古墳}} (in Tenri City, Kayashō Town) is strongly supported{{Sfn|天理の古墳100|2015|p=55}}, while alternative theories propose that the true interred of this tumulus is {{ill|Toyo (queen)|ja|台与|lt=Queen Toyo}}, a successor to {{ill|Himiko|ja|卑弥呼}} (who may have been enshrined in the Hashihaka Kofun){{R|白石}}. [[category:New pages]][[ja:西殿塚古墳]] == Burial == The interred individual is not definitively known, but the site is officially designated as the resting place of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|ja|手白香皇女}}. However, the construction date (3rd century) conflicts with Princess Tashiraka’s presumed era (6th century), leading some to propose the nearby {{ill|Nishiyamazuka Kofun|ja|西山塚古墳}} as her true mausoleum.{{Sfn|天理の古墳100|2015|p=55}} Other theories suggest Queen {{ill|Himiko|ja|卑弥呼}}’s successor, {{ill|Toyo (queen)|ja|台与|lt=Queen Toyo}}, or [[Emperor Sujin]] as the interred individual.{{Sfn|白石太一郎|2013|pp=171-174}} == Site History == * {{ill|1876|ja|1876年}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治}} 9), designated as the mausoleum of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|lt=Tebarakakōjo|ja|手白香皇女}}{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 陵墓篇 第65号|2014|pp=108-112}}. * {{ill|1889|ja|1889年}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治}} 22), repaired and maintained as a mausoleum {{ill|Kinuta Tomb|ja|衾田陵（国史）}}. * {{ill|1986|ja|1986年}} period ({{ill|Shōwa|ja|昭和}} 61 fiscal year), the first survey was conducted{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=1-4}}. * {{ill|1989|ja|1989年}} period ({{ill|Heisei|ja|平成}} first fiscal year), an exterior survey of the tumulus was carried out by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency Shoryo Department|ja|宮内庁書陵部}} {{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991|pp=100-111}}. * From {{ill|1992|ja|1992年|lt=1992|lt_ja=1992}} to {{ill|1994|ja|1994年}}, ({{ill|Heisei|ja|平成}} 4–6 fiscal years), the 2nd to 4th surveys were conducted by the Tenri City Board of Education{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=1-4}}. * {{ill|2012|ja|2012年}} ({{ill|Heisei|ja|平成}} 24): ** On April 9, an aerial 3D survey was conducted by the {{ill|Nara Prefectural Kashihara Archaeological Institute|ja|奈良県立橿原考古学研究所}} and {{ill|Asia Aerial Surveying|ja|アジア航測}}{{PDFlink|[http://www.ajiko.co.jp/news/2012/hashihaka_rittaichizu.pdf "Creation of a Red-colored 3D Map of the Hashihaka and Seidenzuka Kofun"]}} (Press release from the Nara Prefectural Kashihara Archaeological Institute and Asia Aerial Surveying Co., Ltd., 2012).[https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXNASDG0503K_V00C12A6CR8000/ "Himiko’s Tomb? 3D Helicopter Survey of the Hashihaka Kofun by Kashihara Institute, etc."] (Nikkei, June 5, 2012).. ** In August, following a theft incident (with no destruction of the remains) and subsequent restoration, a survey was carried out by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency Shoryo Department|ja|宮内庁書陵部}} {{Sfn|書陵部紀要 陵墓篇 第65号|2014|pp=108-112}}. * {{ill|2013|ja|2013年}} ({{ill|Heisei|ja|平成}} 25) on February 20, an on-site survey was conducted by representatives of 15 academic societies in archaeology and history[https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXNASDG1905C_Q3A220C1CR0000/ "Himiko’s Tomb? First On-site Survey at the Hashihaka Kofun in Nara, Raising Expectations for Research Progress"] (Nikkei, February 20, 2013).. == Tumulus == [[File:Tonotono-tsuka stereo.jpg|thumb|{{center|Nishitonozuka Kofun's {{ill|Stereogram|ja|ステレオグラム|lt=Stereogram|lt_ja=ステレオ}} Aerial Photograph (1979) In the image, the {{ill|Higashidenzuka Kofun|ja|東殿塚古墳|1=Higashitonotsuka Kofun}} is shown at the top and the {{ill|Seidenzuka Kofun|ja|西殿塚古墳|1=Nishitonozuka Kofun}} at the bottom. {{ill|National Aerial Photography|ja|国土航空写真}}.]] The dimensions of the tumulus are as follows{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=5-7}}. * Tumulus length: approximately 230 meters (in some sources, 234 meters{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}, 220 meters{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 陵墓篇 第65号|2014|pp=108-112}}, or 219 meters{{R|堺市}}). * Posterior circular portion – built with 3 tiers on the east side and 4 tiers on the west side. ** Diameter: approximately 140 meters ** Height: approximately 16 meters (east side) * Anterior portion – built with 1 tier on the east side and 2 tiers on the west side. ** Width: approximately 130 meters ** Height: approximately 12 meters (east side) * Square platform (mound) – built in one tier. ** Posterior circular portion: 25.15 meters east–west, 26.54 meters north–south, height 3.00 meters{{R|2012年報道発表資料}} ** Anterior portion: 12.92 meters east–west, 14.43 meters north–south, height 1.87 meters{{R|2012年報道発表資料}} In the theory where the tumulus length is taken as 219 meters, it ranks as the 24th largest in the country{{R|堺市}}. The tiered terraces of the tumulus do not directly connect the posterior circular and anterior portions; the difference in tiers between these portions is reconciled in the constricted section{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991|pp=100-111}}. Furthermore, on the western side of the tumulus, a broad, flat surface (apron), characteristic of the Nishitonozuka Kofun, has been shaped as the lowest tier{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=5-7}}. On the eastern side of the tumulus, there are two bridge-like structures located in the central area of the posterior circular portion and on the southern side of the anterior portion, both of which connect to the adjacent {{ill|Higashidenzuka Kofun|ja|東殿塚古墳|1=Higashitonotsuka Kofun}}{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=5-7}}. == Interred ==
'''Family Tree Based on the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}}'''The reign information is based on the {{ill|Nihon Jinmei Daijiten|ja|日本人名大辞典}} (Kodansha). {{familytree/start|style="text-align:left; font-size:100%"}} {{familytree|border=0|||||01| 01={{sup|24}} {{ill|Emperor Ninken|ja|仁賢天皇}}
{{small|(Reign: end of 5th century)}}}} {{familytree|border=0|||||||)|.}} {{familytree|border=0|01|y|02|03| 01={{sup|26}} {{ill|Emperor Keitai|ja|継体天皇}}
{{small|(Reign: 507?-531?)}}|02={{ill|Princess Tashiraka|lt=Tebarakakōjo|ja|手白香皇女}}|03={{sup|25}} {{ill|Emperor Buretsu|ja|武烈天皇}}
{{small|(Reign: end of 5th century – early 6th century)}}}} {{familytree|border=0||||01|| 01={{sup|29}} {{ill|Emperor Kinmei|ja|欽明天皇}}
{{small|(Reign: 539?-571?)}}}} {{familytree/end}}
The actual interred of the {{ill|Seidenzuka Kofun|ja|西殿塚古墳|1=Nishitonozuka Kofun}} remains unclear; however, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|ja|宮内庁}} designates it as the mausoleum of the 26th {{ill|Emperor Keitai|ja|継体天皇}}’s consort, '''{{ill|Princess Tashiraka|lt=Tebarakakōjo|ja|手白香皇女}}''' (Tashiraka no Hime-miko, also rendered as Tashiraka no Hairarō/ Tashiraka no Himemi){{Sfn|衾田陵（国史）}}Compiled by the Imperial Ministry of Mausolea [{{NDLDC|1237123/11}} "Guide to Mausolea"] (1934, National Diet Library Digital Collection), 11 panels."Compilation of Mausoleum Topographical Maps, Abbreviated Edition", compiled by the Imperial Household Agency Shoryo Department Mausoleum Section, [[Gakuseisha]], 2014, p. 406.. Although the mausoleum of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|lt=Tebarakakōjo|ja|手白香皇女}} is not mentioned in either the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} or the {{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}}, in the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式}}’s mausolea section (displayed as {{ill|Shoryo Department|ja|諸陵寮}}) it is recorded as the distant "Kinuta Tomb". It is said to be located in {{ill|Yamato Province|ja|大和国}}’s {{ill|Yamabe District|ja|山辺郡}}, covering an area of two chō east–west and two chō north–south, with no separate guard door, the mound door of the Kamikami Burial Mound of Yamabe (the mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Sushin|ja|崇神天皇}}) concurrently serving as its guard{{Sfn|衾田陵（国史）}}. Later, during the {{ill|Medieval period|ja|中世}}, the traditional accounts regarding the location of the mausoleum were lost{{Sfn|衾田陵（国史）}}. In {{ill|1876|ja|1876年}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治}} 9), the {{ill|Kyōbushō|ja|教部省}} designated the {{ill|Seidenzuka Kofun|ja|西殿塚古墳|1=Nishitonozuka Kofun}} as the mausoleum, and in {{ill|1889|ja|1889年}} ({{ill|Meiji|ja|明治}} 22) repairs were carried out{{Sfn|衾田陵（国史）}}. [[File:Hashihaka-kofun zenkei.JPG|サムネイル|220px|{{center|{{ill|Hashihaka Kofun|ja|箸墓古墳}} (located in {{ill|Sakurai City|ja|桜井市}}, Hashinaka)}}{{small|Attributed to {{ill|Wajishiki no Hime|ja|倭迹迹日百襲姫命}}. Archaeologically, it is considered either the tomb of the first great king of the {{ill|Yamato Kingdom|ja|ヤマト王権}} or the tomb of {{ill|Himiko|ja|卑弥呼}}.}}]] On the other hand, regarding the true mausoleum of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|lt=Tebarakakōjo|ja|手白香皇女}}, a prevailing theory holds that it should be identified not with the Nishitonozuka Kofun but with the {{ill|Nishiyamazuka Kofun|ja|西山塚古墳}} (located in Tenri City, Kayashō Town){{Sfn|天理の古墳100|2015|p=55}}. This theory is based on the fact that while the construction date of the Nishitonozuka Kofun is estimated to be around the latter half of the 3rd century, the date for the Nishiyamazuka Kofun is around the {{ill|6th century|ja|6世紀}}, which corresponds with the assumed period for {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|lt=Tebarakakōjo|ja|手白香皇女}}{{Sfn|天理の古墳100|2015|p=55}}. Meanwhile, as for the true interred of the Nishitonozuka Kofun, some theories propose that it is {{ill|Daiyo|ja|台与}} (also written 壹與/臺與), based on its subsequent position to the {{ill|Hashihaka Kofun|ja|箸墓古墳}}—regarded as the tomb of {{ill|Himiko|ja|卑弥呼}}—or that it is {{ill|Emperor Sushin|ja|崇神天皇}}{{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, ''The Formation and Development of the Wa Kingdom as Seen from the Kofun'', Keibunsha, 2013, pp. 171-174.,{{ill|Suiz Wada|ja|和田萃}} “On the Yamabe Road”, in ''The Ancient History of Mount Miwa'', Gakuseisha, 2003. among others. {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%" |+ Estimated Early Great King Tombs of the Yamato Kingdom
{{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎}}, ''The Formation and Development of the Wa Kingdom as Seen from the Kofun'' (日本歴史 私の最新講義), Keibunsha, 2013, pp. 181-186. ! Order !! Tumulus Name |- |1||{{ill|Hashihaka Kofun|ja|箸墓古墳}} |- |2||'''{{ill|Nishitonozuka Kofun|ja|西殿塚古墳|1=Nishitonozuka Kofun}}''' |- |3||{{ill|Sakurai Chausuyama Kofun|ja|桜井茶臼山古墳|lt=Sakurai Chausuyama Kofun|lt_ja=外山茶臼山古墳}} |- |4||{{ill|Mesuriyama Kofun|ja|メスリ山古墳}} |- |5||{{ill|Andonyama Kofun|ja|行燈山古墳}} |- |6||{{ill|Shibuya Mukaeyama Kofun|ja|渋谷向山古墳}} |} == References == {{Reflist|2}} == Further Reading == * Site explanation board, Tenri City Board of Education, 2010. * {{Cite book|和書|title=Nishitonozuka Kofun and Higashitonozuka Kofun (Tenri City Cultural Heritage Report No.7)|publisher=Tenri City Board of Education|year=2000|ref={{Harvid|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|title=100 Kofun in Tenri|publisher=Tenri City Board of Education|year=2015|ref={{Harvid|天理の古墳100|2015}}}} == Related Articles == * {{ill|Yamato Kofun Group|ja|大和古墳群|1=Ōyamato Kofun Group}} * {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|ja|手白香皇女}} == External Links == * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/miryoku/tenrinomiryoku1/kofun/1445323092951.html Nishitonozuka Kofun -
