Height approximately 16m (rear circle) |built = Late {{ill|3rd century|en|3rd century|WD=Q8101|lt=3rd century|1=3rd century}} to its end |burial = Unknown |Interred = ({{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} Historic Site) {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|en|Princess Tashiraka|WD=Q11075749|lt=Princess Tashiraka|1=Princess Tashiraka}}
(One theory) {{ill|Toyo (queen)|en|Toyo (queen)|WD=Q5358937|lt=Queen Himiko|1=Toyo (queen)}}
(Another theory) Emperor {{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|WD=Q333530|lt=Sujin|1=Emperor Sujin}} |burial goods = {{ill|Special pedestal and pottery|ja|特殊器台・特殊壺|1=Ceremonial vessel stands or jars|1=Ceremonial vessel stands or jars|lt=Special plattypes and jars|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Special pedestal and pottery|13=User:Immanuelle/Ceremonial vessel stands or jars|qq=}}, Miyama-style special pedestals and pottery
Ordinary cylindrical haniwa |Mausoleum = {{ill|Fusumada Mausoleum|ja|衾田陵|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fusumada Mausoleum|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Historic Site1 by the Imperial Household Agency) |notes = Ranked 24th nationwide by size
(if mound length is considered 219m)[https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/Ranking/zenkoku.html Ranking of Kofun areas in Japan] (Sakai City website, updated May 13, 2018).
Considered the royal tomb following {{ill|Hashihaka Kofun|en|Hashihaka Kofun|WD=Q11603420|lt=Hashihaka Kofun|1=Hashihaka Kofun}} |map = Japan Nara |map_dot_label = Nishitonozuka Kofun |map_dot_label = Top |type = Keyhole-shaped tomb - South |architectural_styles = {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|WD=Q11268718|1=Zenpōkōenfun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳}} |commemorates = {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|WD=Q11075749|1=Princess Tashiraka}} }} [[File:Nishitonotsuka Kofun, haisho.jpg|thumb|220px|{{center|{{ill|Princess Tashiraka|en|Princess Tashiraka|WD=Q11075749|lt=Princess Tashiraka|1=Princess Tashiraka}} Fusumada Mausoleum {{ill|Haisho|ja|拝所|lt=Worship Site|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Haisho|qq=}}}}]] '''Nishitonozuka Kofun''' (西殿塚古墳) is a {{ill|Kofun|en|Kofun|WD=Q1141225|lt=Kofun|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Tenri, Nara|en|Tenri, Nara|WD=Q502196|lt=Tenri, Nara Prefecture|1=Tenri, Nara}}, Nakayama Town. It is a {{ill|Zenpōkōenfun|en|Zenpōkōenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpōkōenfun|1=Zenpōkōenfun}} and part of the {{ill|Ōyamato Kofun Cluster|ja|大和古墳群|1=Ōyamato Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamato Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamato Kofun Cluster|qq=}} (Nakayama subgroup). The identity of the interred is uncertain, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} designates the site as the '''Fusumada Mausoleum''' (衾田陵), the resting place of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|en|Princess Tashiraka|WD=Q11075749|lt=Princess Tashiraka|1=Princess Tashiraka}}, the consort of {{ill|Emperor Keitai|en|Emperor Keitai|WD=Q349277|lt=Emperor Keitai|1=Emperor Keitai}} It is estimated to have been built in the latter half of the {{ill|3rd century|en|3rd century|WD=Q8101|lt=3rd century|1=3rd century}} (early {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|WD=Q459939|lt=Kofun period|1=Kofun period}}) and is considered the royal tomb succeeding the earliest keyhole-shaped tomb, the {{ill|Hashihaka Kofun|en|Hashihaka Kofun|WD=Q11603420|lt=Hashihaka Kofun|1=Hashihaka Kofun}}. == Overview == It is a gigantic keyhole-shaped tumulus constructed on the hilly area along the eastern edge of the {{ill|Nara Basin|en|Nara Basin|WD=Q10942269|lt=Nara Basin|1=Nara Basin}}. Adjacent to its eastern side is the {{ill|Higashitonotsuka Kofun|ja|東殿塚古墳|1=Higashitonotsuka Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Higashitonotsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Higashitonotsuka Kofun|qq=}}, and these two, being at the highest point within the {{ill|Ōyamato Kofun Cluster|ja|大和古墳群|1=Ōyamato Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamato Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamato Kofun Cluster|qq=}}, offer a panoramic view of the entire basinHistoric Site Explanation Board.{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 陵墓篇 第65号|2014|pp=108-112}}. The tumulus has remained well preserved to the present day{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991|pp=100-111}}. It is currently managed by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} as the mausoleum of an empress under its jurisdiction; to date, exterior investigations of the tumulus have been conducted by the {{ill|Archives and Mausolea Department|en|Archives and Mausolea Department|WD=Q4346533|lt=Archives and Mausolea Department|1=Archives and Mausolea Department}} during the {{ill|1989|en|1989|WD=Q2425|lt=1989|1=1989}} ({{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|WD=Q234510|lt=Heisei|1=Heisei era}} first fiscal year) period{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991|pp=100-111}}, surveys of the surrounding area by the Tenri City Board of Education during the {{ill|1992|en|1992|WD=Q2060|lt=1992|1=1992}}–{{ill|1994|en|1994|WD=Q2067|lt=1994|1=1994}} period (Heisei 4–6 fiscal years){{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=1-4}}, and an academic on-site survey in the {{ill|2012|en|2012|WD=Q1990|lt=2012|1=2012}} period (Heisei 24 fiscal year){{R|2013rd year 調査}}. The tumulus is of a keyhole type with its anterior portion facing south; however, because it was constructed at a right angle to a sloping terrain (with the higher elevation on the east side), it takes on an asymmetrical type{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}. In the posterior circular portion, it is built with three tiers on the east side and four tiers on the west side, while in the anterior portion it is built with one tier on the east side and two tiers on the west side{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=5-7}}. The overall length of the tumulus measures about 230 {{ill|Metre|en|Metre|WD=Q11573|lt=meters|1=Metre}}, making it the largest within the Ōyamato Kofun Cluster. On its exterior, in addition to the presence of {{ill|Fukiishi|en|Fukiishi|WD=Q11621213|lt=Fukiishi|1=Fukiishi}}, early haniwa have been detected around the tumulus, including {{ill|Special plattypes and jars|ja|特殊器台・特殊壺|1=Ceremonial vessel stands or jars|1=Ceremonial vessel stands or jars|lt=Special Kiderai-type earthenware, special Kiderai-type haniwa, special tsubo-shaped haniwa|lt_ja=特殊器台形土器・特殊器台形埴輪・特殊壺形埴輪|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Special plattypes and jars|13=User:Immanuelle/Ceremonial vessel stands or jars|qq=}} (from the tumulus itself) and {{ill|Cylindrical Haniwa|ja|円筒埴輪|lt=cylindrical haniwa|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Cylindrical Haniwa|qq=}} with a stepped neck{{R|説明板}}. Although the burial facilities remain unclear, square plattypes (mounds) are present on both the posterior and anterior portions of the tumulus{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=5-7}}. This Nishitonozuka Kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the latter half of the {{ill|3rd century|en|3rd century|WD=Q8101|lt=3rd century|1=3rd century}} during the early part of the {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|WD=Q459939|lt=Kofun period|1=Kofun period}}{{R|説明板}}[http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/miryoku/tenrinomiryoku1/kofun/1445323092951.html]{{ill|Nishitonozuka Kofun|ja|西殿塚古墳|1=Nishitonozuka Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitonozuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitonozuka Kofun|qq=}} (Tenri City Homepage). It is regarded as the great tomb of the Yamato Kingdom that succeeded the {{ill|Hashihaka Kofun|en|Hashihaka Kofun|WD=Q11603420|lt=Hashihaka Kofun|1=Hashihaka Kofun}} (located in {{ill|Sakurai, Nara|en|Sakurai, Nara|WD=Q127026|lt=Sakurai City|1=Sakurai, Nara}} Hashinaka){{R|白石}}, and in conjunction with the adjacent {{ill|Higaida-ōtsuka Kofun|ja|東殿塚古墳|1=Higashitonotsuka Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Higaida-ōtsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Higashitonotsuka Kofun|qq=}}, it is considered to be part of a continuous construction sequence beginning with Nishitonozuka Kofun{{R|説明板}}. Although the identity of the interred remains unclear, it is currently Historic Site1 by the Imperial Household Agency as the mausoleum of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|en|Princess Tashiraka|WD=Q11075749|lt=Tebarakakōjo|1=Princess Tashiraka}} (the {{ill|Empress|ja|皇后|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Empress|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=Empress consort|WD=Q7723211}} of the 26th {{ill|Emperor Keitai|en|Emperor Keitai|WD=Q349277|lt=Emperor Keitai|1=Emperor Keitai}} ){{Sfn|衾田陵（国史）}}. However, since the construction date does not correspond with the assumed period of the {{ill|6th century|en|6th century|WD=Q8090|lt=6th century|1=6th century}} for {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|en|Princess Tashiraka|WD=Q11075749|lt=Tebarakakōjo|1=Princess Tashiraka}}, a theory that the true mausoleum of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|en|Princess Tashiraka|WD=Q11075749|lt=Tebarakakōjo|1=Princess Tashiraka}} is the {{ill|Nishiyamazuka Kofun|ja|西山塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishiyamazuka Kofun|qq=}} (in Tenri City, Kayashō Town) is strongly supported{{Sfn|天理の古墳100|2015|p=55}}, while alternative theories propose that the true interred of this tumulus is {{ill|Toyo (queen)|en|Toyo (queen)|WD=Q5358937|lt=Queen Toyo|1=Toyo (queen)}}, a successor to {{ill|Himiko|en|Himiko|WD=Q234451|lt=Himiko|1=Himiko}} (who may have been enshrined in the Hashihaka Kofun){{R|白石}}. == burial == The interred individual is not definitively known, but the site is officially Historic Site1 as the resting place of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|en|Princess Tashiraka|WD=Q11075749|lt=Princess Tashiraka|1=Princess Tashiraka}}. However, the construction date (3rd century) conflicts with Princess Tashiraka’s presumed era (6th century), leading some to propose the nearby {{ill|Nishiyamazuka Kofun|ja|西山塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishiyamazuka Kofun|qq=}} as her true mausoleum.{{Sfn|天理の古墳100|2015|p=55}} Other theories suggest Queen {{ill|Himiko|en|Himiko|WD=Q234451|lt=Himiko|1=Himiko}}’s successor, {{ill|Toyo (queen)|en|Toyo (queen)|WD=Q5358937|lt=Queen Toyo|1=Toyo (queen)}}, or {{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|WD=Q333530|lt=Emperor Sujin|1=Emperor Sujin}} as the interred individual.{{Sfn|白石太一郎|2013|pp=171-174}} == Site History == * {{ill|1876|en|1876|WD=Q7766|lt=1876|1=1876}} ({{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era|1=Meiji era}} 9), Historic Site1 as the mausoleum of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|en|Princess Tashiraka|WD=Q11075749|lt=Tebarakakōjo|1=Princess Tashiraka}}{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 陵墓篇 第65号|2014|pp=108-112}}. * {{ill|1889|en|1889|WD=Q7831|lt=1889|1=1889}} ({{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era|1=Meiji era}} 22), repaired and maintained as a mausoleum {{ill|Kinuta Tomb|ja|衾田陵（国史）|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinuta Tomb|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. * {{ill|1986|en|1986|WD=Q2430|lt=1986|1=1986}} period ({{ill|Shōwa era|en|Shōwa era|WD=Q327567|lt=Shōwa|1=Shōwa era}} 61 fiscal year), the first survey was conducted{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=1-4}}. * {{ill|1989|en|1989|WD=Q2425|lt=1989|1=1989}} period ({{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|WD=Q234510|lt=Heisei|1=Heisei era}} first fiscal year), an exterior survey of the tumulus was carried out by the {{ill|Archives and Mausolea Department|en|Archives and Mausolea Department|WD=Q4346533|lt=Archives and Mausolea Department|1=Archives and Mausolea Department}} {{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991|pp=100-111}}. * From {{ill|1992|en|1992|WD=Q2060|lt=1992|1=1992}} to {{ill|1994|en|1994|WD=Q2067|lt=1994|1=1994}}, ({{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|WD=Q234510|lt=Heisei|1=Heisei era}} 4–6 fiscal years), the 2nd to 4th surveys were conducted by the Tenri City Board of Education{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=1-4}}. * {{ill|2012|en|2012|WD=Q1990|lt=2012|1=2012}} ({{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|WD=Q234510|lt=Heisei|1=Heisei era}} 24): ** On April 9, an aerial 3D survey was conducted by the {{ill|The Museum, Archaeological Institute of Kashihara, Nara Prefecture|en|The Museum, Archaeological Institute of Kashihara, Nara Prefecture|WD=Q112961122|lt=Kashihara Archaeological Institute|1=The Museum, Archaeological Institute of Kashihara, Nara Prefecture}} and {{ill|Asia Aerial Surveying|ja|アジア航測|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Asia Aerial Surveying|1=Asia Air Survey|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11283384}}{{PDFlink|[http://www.ajiko.co.jp/news/2012/hashihaka_rittaichizu.pdf "Creation of a Red-colored 3D map of the Hashihaka and Seidenzuka Kofun"]}} (Press release from the Nara Prefectural Kashihara Archaeological Institute and Asia Aerial Surveying Co., Ltd., 2012).[https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXNASDG0503K_V00C12A6CR8000/ "Himiko’s Tomb? 3D Helicopter Survey of the Hashihaka Kofun by Kashihara Institute, etc."] (Nikkei, June 5, 2012).. ** In August, following a theft incident (with no destruction of the remains) and subsequent restoration, a survey was carried out by the {{ill|Archives and Mausolea Department|en|Archives and Mausolea Department|WD=Q4346533|lt=Archives and Mausolea Department|1=Archives and Mausolea Department}} {{Sfn|書陵部紀要 陵墓篇 第65号|2014|pp=108-112}}. * {{ill|2013|en|2013|WD=Q1998|lt=2013|1=2013}} ({{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|WD=Q234510|lt=Heisei|1=Heisei era}} 25) on February 20, an on-site survey was conducted by representatives of 15 academic societies in archaeology and history[https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXNASDG1905C_Q3A220C1CR0000/ "Himiko’s Tomb? First On-site Survey at the Hashihaka Kofun in Nara, Raising Expectations for Research Progress"] (Nikkei, February 20, 2013).. == Kofun == [[File:Tonotono-tsuka stereo.jpg|thumb|{{center|Nishitonozuka Kofun's {{ill|Stereogram|ja|ステレオグラム|lt=Stereogram|lt_ja=ステレオ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Stereogram|1=Stereogram|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1083936}} Aerial Photograph (1979) In the image, the {{ill|Higashidenzuka Kofun|ja|東殿塚古墳|1=Higashitonotsuka Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Higashidenzuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Higashitonotsuka Kofun|qq=}} is shown at the top and the {{ill|Seidenzuka Kofun|ja|西殿塚古墳|1=Nishitonozuka Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Seidenzuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitonozuka Kofun|qq=}} at the bottom. {{ill|National Aerial Photography|ja|国土航空写真|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Aerial Photography|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135491397|1=Geospatial Information Authority of Japan}}.]] The area of the tumulus are as follows{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=5-7}}. * Kofun length: approximately 230 meters (in some sources, 234 meters{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}, 220 meters{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 陵墓篇 第65号|2014|pp=108-112}}, or 219 meters{{R|堺市}}). * Posterior circular portion – built with 3 tiers on the east side and 4 tiers on the west side. ** Diameter: approximately 140 meters ** Height: approximately 16 meters (east side) * Anterior portion – built with 1 tier on the east side and 2 tiers on the west side. ** Width: approximately 130 meters ** Height: approximately 12 meters (east side) * Square plattype (mound) – built in one tier. ** Posterior circular portion: 25.15 meters east–west, 26.54 meters north–south, height 3.00 meters{{R|2012nd year 報道発表資料}} ** Anterior portion: 12.92 meters east–west, 14.43 meters north–south, height 1.87 meters{{R|2012nd year 報道発表資料}} In the theory where the tumulus length is taken as 219 meters, it Ranks as the 24th largest in the country{{R|堺市}}. The tiered terraces of the tumulus do not directly connect the posterior circular and anterior portions; the difference in tiers between these portions is reconciled in the constricted section{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991|pp=100-111}}. Furthermore, on the western side of the tumulus, a broad, flat surface (apron), characteristic of the Nishitonozuka Kofun, has been shaped as the lowest tier{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=5-7}}. On the eastern side of the tumulus, there are two bridge-like structures located in the central area of the posterior circular portion and on the southern side of the anterior portion, both of which connect to the adjacent {{ill|Higashidenzuka Kofun|ja|東殿塚古墳|1=Higashitonotsuka Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Higashidenzuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Higashitonotsuka Kofun|qq=}}{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=5-7}}. == Interred ==
'''Family Tree Based on the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|WD=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki|1=Nihon Shoki}}'''The reign intypeation is based on the {{ill|Nihon Jinmei Daijiten|ja|日本人名大辞典|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nihon Jinmei Daijiten|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Kodansha). {{familytree/start|style="text-align:left; font-size:100%"}} {{familytree|border=0|||||01| 01={{sup|24}} {{ill|Emperor Ninken|en|Emperor Ninken|WD=Q357266|lt=Emperor Ninken|1=Emperor Ninken}}
{{small|(Reign: end of 5th century)}}}} {{familytree|border=0|||||||)|.}} {{familytree|border=0|01|y|02|03| 01={{sup|26}} {{ill|Emperor Keitai|en|Emperor Keitai|WD=Q349277|lt=Emperor Keitai|1=Emperor Keitai}}
{{small|(Reign: 507?-531?)}}|02={{ill|Princess Tashiraka|en|Princess Tashiraka|WD=Q11075749|lt=Tebarakakōjo|1=Princess Tashiraka}}|03={{sup|25}} {{ill|Emperor Buretsu|en|Emperor Buretsu|WD=Q334644|lt=Emperor Buretsu|1=Emperor Buretsu}}
{{small|(Reign: end of 5th century – early 6th century)}}}} {{familytree|border=0||||01|| 01={{sup|29}} {{ill|Emperor Kinmei|en|Emperor Kinmei|WD=Q329792|lt=Emperor Kinmei|1=Emperor Kinmei}}
{{small|(Reign: 539?-571?)}}}} {{familytree/end}}
The actual interred of the {{ill|Seidenzuka Kofun|ja|西殿塚古墳|1=Nishitonozuka Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Seidenzuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitonozuka Kofun|qq=}} remains unclear; however, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} designates it as the mausoleum of the 26th {{ill|Emperor Keitai|en|Emperor Keitai|WD=Q349277|lt=Emperor Keitai|1=Emperor Keitai}}’s consort, '''{{ill|Princess Tashiraka|en|Princess Tashiraka|WD=Q11075749|lt=Tebarakakōjo|1=Princess Tashiraka}}''' (Tashiraka no Hime-miko, also rendered as Tashiraka no Hairarō/ Tashiraka no Himemi){{Sfn|衾田陵（国史）}}Compiled by the Imperial Ministry of Mausolea [{{NDLDC|1237123/11}} "Guide to Mausolea"] (1934, National Diet Library Digital Collection), 11 panels."Compilation of Mausoleum Topographical maps, Abbreviated Edition", compiled by the Imperial Household Agency Shoryo Department Mausoleum Section, [[Gakuseisha]], 2014, p. 406.. Although the mausoleum of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|en|Princess Tashiraka|WD=Q11075749|lt=Tebarakakōjo|1=Princess Tashiraka}} is not mentioned in either the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|WD=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki|1=Nihon Shoki}} or the {{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|WD=Q813031|lt=Kojiki|1=Kojiki}}, in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|Engishiki|WD=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki|1=Engishiki}}’s mausolea section (displayed as {{ill|Shoryo Department|ja|諸陵寮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shoryo Department|1=Shoryō-ryō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11632153}}) it is recorded as the distant "Kinuta Tomb". It is said to be located in {{ill|Yamato Province|en|Yamato Province|WD=Q907495|lt=Yamato Province|1=Yamato Province}}’s {{ill|Yamabe District, Nara|en|Yamabe District, Nara|WD=Q1130739|lt=Yamabe District|1=Yamabe District, Nara}}, covering an area of two chō east–west and two chō north–south, with no separate guard door, the mound door of the Kamikami Kofun of Yamabe (the mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|WD=Q333530|lt=Emperor Sushin|1=Emperor Sujin}}) concurrently serving as its guard{{Sfn|衾田陵（国史）}}. Later, during the {{ill|Middle Ages|en|Middle Ages|WD=Q12554|lt=Medieval period|1=Middle Ages}}, the traditional accounts regarding the location of the mausoleum were lost{{Sfn|衾田陵（国史）}}. In {{ill|1876|en|1876|WD=Q7766|lt=1876|1=1876}} ({{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era|1=Meiji era}} 9), the {{ill|Ministry of Religion (Japan)|en|Ministry of Religion (Japan)|WD=Q4294653|lt=Ministry of Religion|1=Ministry of Religion (Japan)}} Historic Site1 the {{ill|Seidenzuka Kofun|ja|西殿塚古墳|1=Nishitonozuka Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Seidenzuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitonozuka Kofun|qq=}} as the mausoleum, and in {{ill|1889|en|1889|WD=Q7831|lt=1889|1=1889}} ({{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era|1=Meiji era}} 22) repairs were carried out{{Sfn|衾田陵（国史）}}. [[File:Hashihaka-kofun zenkei.JPG|サムネイル|220px|{{center|{{ill|Hashihaka Kofun|en|Hashihaka Kofun|WD=Q11603420|lt=Hashihaka Kofun|1=Hashihaka Kofun}} (located in {{ill|Sakurai, Nara|en|Sakurai, Nara|WD=Q127026|lt=Sakurai City|1=Sakurai, Nara}}, Hashinaka)}}{{small|Attributed to {{ill|Princess Yamato Totohi Momoso|en|Princess Yamato Totohi Momoso|WD=Q11387098|lt=Wajishiki no Hime|1=Yamato-totohi-momoso-hime}}. Archaeologically, it is considered either the tomb of the first great king of the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|en|Yamato Kingship|WD=Q2658252|lt=Yamato Kingdom|1=Yamato Kingship}} or the tomb of {{ill|Himiko|en|Himiko|WD=Q234451|lt=Himiko|1=Himiko}}.}}]] On the other hand, regarding the true mausoleum of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|en|Princess Tashiraka|WD=Q11075749|lt=Tebarakakōjo|1=Princess Tashiraka}}, a prevailing theory holds that it should be identified not with the Nishitonozuka Kofun but with the {{ill|Nishiyamazuka Kofun|ja|西山塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishiyamazuka Kofun|qq=}} (located in Tenri City, Kayashō Town){{Sfn|天理の古墳100|2015|p=55}}. This theory is based on the fact that while the construction date of the Nishitonozuka Kofun is estimated to be around the latter half of the 3rd century, the date for the Nishiyamazuka Kofun is around the {{ill|6th century|en|6th century|WD=Q8090|lt=6th century|1=6th century}}, which corresponds with the assumed period for {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|en|Princess Tashiraka|WD=Q11075749|lt=Tebarakakōjo|1=Princess Tashiraka}}{{Sfn|天理の古墳100|2015|p=55}}. Meanwhile, as for the true interred of the Nishitonozuka Kofun, some theories propose that it is {{ill|Toyo (queen)|en|Toyo (queen)|WD=Q5358937|lt=Daiyo|1=Toyo (queen)}} (also written 壹與/臺與), based on its subsequent position to the {{ill|Hashihaka Kofun|en|Hashihaka Kofun|WD=Q11603420|lt=Hashihaka Kofun|1=Hashihaka Kofun}}—regarded as the tomb of {{ill|Himiko|en|Himiko|WD=Q234451|lt=Himiko|1=Himiko}}—or that it is {{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|WD=Q333530|lt=Emperor Sushin|1=Emperor Sujin}}{{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|1=Shiraishi Taichiro|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11580156}}, ''The Formation and Development of the Wa Kingdom as Seen from the Kofun'', Keibunsha, 2013, pp. 171-174.,{{ill|Suiz Wada|ja|和田萃|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suiz Wada|1=Atsumu Wada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11418120}} “On the Yamabe Road”, in ''The Ancient History of Mount Miwa'', Gakuseisha, 2003. among others. {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%" |+ Estimated Early Great King Tombs of the Yamato Kingdom
{{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|1=Shiraishi Taichiro|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11580156}}, ''The Formation and Development of the Wa Kingdom as Seen from the Kofun'' (日本歴史 私の最新講義), Keibunsha, 2013, pp. 181-186. ! Order !! Height approximately 16m (rear circle) |built = Late {{ill|3rd century|en|3rd century|WD=Q8101|lt=3rd century|1=3rd century}} to its end |burial = Unknown |Interred = ({{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} Historic Site) {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|en|Princess Tashiraka|WD=Q11075749|lt=Princess Tashiraka|1=Princess Tashiraka}}
(One theory) {{ill|Toyo (queen)|en|Toyo (queen)|WD=Q5358937|lt=Queen Himiko|1=Toyo (queen)}}
(Another theory) Emperor {{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|WD=Q333530|lt=Sujin|1=Emperor Sujin}} |burial goods = {{ill|Special pedestal and pottery|ja|特殊器台・特殊壺|1=Ceremonial vessel stands or jars|1=Ceremonial vessel stands or jars|lt=Special plattypes and jars|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Special pedestal and pottery|13=User:Immanuelle/Ceremonial vessel stands or jars|qq=}}, Miyama-style special pedestals and pottery
Ordinary cylindrical haniwa |Mausoleum = {{ill|Fusumada Mausoleum|ja|衾田陵|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fusumada Mausoleum|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Historic Site1 by the Imperial Household Agency) |notes = Ranked 24th nationwide by size
(if mound length is considered 219m)[https://www.city.sakai.lg.jp/kanko/rekishi/dkofun/Ranking/zenkoku.html Ranking of Kofun areas in Japan] (Sakai City website, updated May 13, 2018).
Considered the royal tomb following {{ill|Hashihaka Kofun|en|Hashihaka Kofun|WD=Q11603420|lt=Hashihaka Kofun|1=Hashihaka Kofun}} |map = Japan Nara |map_dot_label = Nishitonozuka Kofun |map_dot_label = Top |type = Keyhole-shaped tomb - South |architectural_styles = {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|WD=Q11268718|1=Zenpō-kōen-fun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳}} |commemorates = {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|WD=Q11075749|1=Princess Tashiraka}} }} [[File:Nishitonotsuka Kofun, haisho.jpg|thumb|220px|{{center|{{ill|Princess Tashiraka|en|Princess Tashiraka|WD=Q11075749|lt=Princess Tashiraka|1=Princess Tashiraka}} Fusumada Mausoleum {{ill|Haisho|ja|拝所|lt=Worship Site|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Haisho|qq=}}}}]] '''Nishitonozuka Kofun''' (西殿塚古墳) is a {{ill|Kofun|en|Kofun|WD=Q1141225|lt=Kofun|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Tenri, Nara|en|Tenri, Nara|WD=Q502196|lt=Tenri, Nara Prefecture|1=Tenri, Nara}}, Nakayama Town. It is a {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|en|Zenpō-kōen-fun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpō-kōen-fun|1=Zenpō-kōen-fun}} and part of the {{ill|Ōyamato Kofun Cluster|ja|大和古墳群|1=Ōyamato Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamato Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamato Kofun Cluster|qq=}} (Nakayama subgroup). The identity of the interred is uncertain, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} designates the site as the '''Fusumada Mausoleum''' (衾田陵), the resting place of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|en|Princess Tashiraka|WD=Q11075749|lt=Princess Tashiraka|1=Princess Tashiraka}}, the consort of {{ill|Emperor Keitai|en|Emperor Keitai|WD=Q349277|lt=Emperor Keitai|1=Emperor Keitai}} It is estimated to have been built in the latter half of the {{ill|3rd century|en|3rd century|WD=Q8101|lt=3rd century|1=3rd century}} (early {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|WD=Q459939|lt=Kofun period|1=Kofun period}}) and is considered the royal tomb succeeding the earliest keyhole-shaped tomb, the {{ill|Hashihaka Kofun|en|Hashihaka Kofun|WD=Q11603420|lt=Hashihaka Kofun|1=Hashihaka Kofun}}. == Overview == It is a gigantic keyhole-shaped tumulus constructed on the hilly area along the eastern edge of the {{ill|Nara Basin|en|Nara Basin|WD=Q10942269|lt=Nara Basin|1=Nara Basin}}. Adjacent to its eastern side is the {{ill|Higashitonotsuka Kofun|ja|東殿塚古墳|1=Higashitonotsuka Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Higashitonotsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Higashitonotsuka Kofun|qq=}}, and these two, being at the highest point within the {{ill|Ōyamato Kofun Cluster|ja|大和古墳群|1=Ōyamato Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamato Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamato Kofun Cluster|qq=}}, offer a panoramic view of the entire basinHistoric Site Explanation Board.{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 陵墓篇 第65号|2014|pp=108-112}}. The tumulus has remained well preserved to the present day{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991|pp=100-111}}. It is currently managed by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} as the mausoleum of an empress under its jurisdiction; to date, exterior investigations of the tumulus have been conducted by the {{ill|Archives and Mausolea Department|en|Archives and Mausolea Department|WD=Q4346533|lt=Archives and Mausolea Department|1=Archives and Mausolea Department}} during the {{ill|1989|en|1989|WD=Q2425|lt=1989|1=1989}} ({{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|WD=Q234510|lt=Heisei|1=Heisei era}} first fiscal year) period{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991|pp=100-111}}, surveys of the surrounding area by the Tenri City Board of Education during the {{ill|1992|en|1992|WD=Q2060|lt=1992|1=1992}}–{{ill|1994|en|1994|WD=Q2067|lt=1994|1=1994}} period (Heisei 4–6 fiscal years){{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=1-4}}, and an academic on-site survey in the {{ill|2012|en|2012|WD=Q1990|lt=2012|1=2012}} period (Heisei 24 fiscal year){{R|2013rd year 調査}}. The tumulus is of a keyhole type with its anterior portion facing south; however, because it was constructed at a right angle to a sloping terrain (with the higher elevation on the east side), it takes on an asymmetrical type{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}. In the posterior circular portion, it is built with three tiers on the east side and four tiers on the west side, while in the anterior portion it is built with one tier on the east side and two tiers on the west side{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=5-7}}. The overall length of the tumulus measures about 230 {{ill|Metre|en|Metre|WD=Q11573|lt=meters|1=Metre}}, making it the largest within the Ōyamato Kofun Cluster. On its exterior, in addition to the presence of {{ill|Fukiishi|en|Fukiishi|WD=Q11621213|lt=Fukiishi|1=Fukiishi}}, early haniwa have been detected around the tumulus, including {{ill|Special plattypes and jars|ja|特殊器台・特殊壺|1=Ceremonial vessel stands or jars|1=Ceremonial vessel stands or jars|lt=Special Kiderai-type earthenware, special Kiderai-type haniwa, special tsubo-shaped haniwa|lt_ja=特殊器台形土器・特殊器台形埴輪・特殊壺形埴輪|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Special plattypes and jars|13=User:Immanuelle/Ceremonial vessel stands or jars|qq=}} (from the tumulus itself) and {{ill|Cylindrical Haniwa|ja|円筒埴輪|lt=cylindrical haniwa|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Cylindrical Haniwa|qq=}} with a stepped neck{{R|説明板}}. Although the burial facilities remain unclear, square plattypes (mounds) are present on both the posterior and anterior portions of the tumulus{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=5-7}}. This Nishitonozuka Kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the latter half of the {{ill|3rd century|en|3rd century|WD=Q8101|lt=3rd century|1=3rd century}} during the early part of the {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|WD=Q459939|lt=Kofun period|1=Kofun period}}{{R|説明板}}[http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/miryoku/tenrinomiryoku1/kofun/1445323092951.html]{{ill|Nishitonozuka Kofun|ja|西殿塚古墳|1=Nishitonozuka Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitonozuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitonozuka Kofun|qq=}} (Tenri City Homepage). It is regarded as the great tomb of the Yamato Kingdom that succeeded the {{ill|Hashihaka Kofun|en|Hashihaka Kofun|WD=Q11603420|lt=Hashihaka Kofun|1=Hashihaka Kofun}} (located in {{ill|Sakurai, Nara|en|Sakurai, Nara|WD=Q127026|lt=Sakurai City|1=Sakurai, Nara}} Hashinaka){{R|白石}}, and in conjunction with the adjacent {{ill|Higaida-ōtsuka Kofun|ja|東殿塚古墳|1=Higashitonotsuka Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Higaida-ōtsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Higashitonotsuka Kofun|qq=}}, it is considered to be part of a continuous construction sequence beginning with Nishitonozuka Kofun{{R|説明板}}. Although the identity of the interred remains unclear, it is currently Historic Site1 by the Imperial Household Agency as the mausoleum of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|en|Princess Tashiraka|WD=Q11075749|lt=Tebarakakōjo|1=Princess Tashiraka}} (the {{ill|Empress|ja|皇后|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Empress|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=Empress consort|WD=Q7723211}} of the 26th {{ill|Emperor Keitai|en|Emperor Keitai|WD=Q349277|lt=Emperor Keitai|1=Emperor Keitai}} ){{Sfn|衾田陵（国史）}}. However, since the construction date does not correspond with the assumed period of the {{ill|6th century|en|6th century|WD=Q8090|lt=6th century|1=6th century}} for {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|en|Princess Tashiraka|WD=Q11075749|lt=Tebarakakōjo|1=Princess Tashiraka}}, a theory that the true mausoleum of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|en|Princess Tashiraka|WD=Q11075749|lt=Tebarakakōjo|1=Princess Tashiraka}} is the {{ill|Nishiyamazuka Kofun|ja|西山塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishiyamazuka Kofun|qq=}} (in Tenri City, Kayashō Town) is strongly supported{{Sfn|天理の古墳100|2015|p=55}}, while alternative theories propose that the true interred of this tumulus is {{ill|Toyo (queen)|en|Toyo (queen)|WD=Q5358937|lt=Queen Toyo|1=Toyo (queen)}}, a successor to {{ill|Himiko|en|Himiko|WD=Q234451|lt=Himiko|1=Himiko}} (who may have been enshrined in the Hashihaka Kofun){{R|白石}}. == burial == The interred individual is not definitively known, but the site is officially Historic Site1 as the resting place of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|en|Princess Tashiraka|WD=Q11075749|lt=Princess Tashiraka|1=Princess Tashiraka}}. However, the construction date (3rd century) conflicts with Princess Tashiraka’s presumed era (6th century), leading some to propose the nearby {{ill|Nishiyamazuka Kofun|ja|西山塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishiyamazuka Kofun|qq=}} as her true mausoleum.{{Sfn|天理の古墳100|2015|p=55}} Other theories suggest Queen {{ill|Himiko|en|Himiko|WD=Q234451|lt=Himiko|1=Himiko}}’s successor, {{ill|Toyo (queen)|en|Toyo (queen)|WD=Q5358937|lt=Queen Toyo|1=Toyo (queen)}}, or {{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|WD=Q333530|lt=Emperor Sujin|1=Emperor Sujin}} as the interred individual.{{Sfn|白石太一郎|2013|pp=171-174}} == Site History == * {{ill|1876|en|1876|WD=Q7766|lt=1876|1=1876}} ({{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era|1=Meiji era}} 9), Historic Site1 as the mausoleum of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|en|Princess Tashiraka|WD=Q11075749|lt=Tebarakakōjo|1=Princess Tashiraka}}{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 陵墓篇 第65号|2014|pp=108-112}}. * {{ill|1889|en|1889|WD=Q7831|lt=1889|1=1889}} ({{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era|1=Meiji era}} 22), repaired and maintained as a mausoleum {{ill|Kinuta Tomb|ja|衾田陵（国史）|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinuta Tomb|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. * {{ill|1986|en|1986|WD=Q2430|lt=1986|1=1986}} period ({{ill|Shōwa era|en|Shōwa era|WD=Q327567|lt=Shōwa|1=Shōwa era}} 61 fiscal year), the first survey was conducted{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=1-4}}. * {{ill|1989|en|1989|WD=Q2425|lt=1989|1=1989}} period ({{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|WD=Q234510|lt=Heisei|1=Heisei era}} first fiscal year), an exterior survey of the tumulus was carried out by the {{ill|Archives and Mausolea Department|en|Archives and Mausolea Department|WD=Q4346533|lt=Archives and Mausolea Department|1=Archives and Mausolea Department}} {{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991|pp=100-111}}. * From {{ill|1992|en|1992|WD=Q2060|lt=1992|1=1992}} to {{ill|1994|en|1994|WD=Q2067|lt=1994|1=1994}}, ({{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|WD=Q234510|lt=Heisei|1=Heisei era}} 4–6 fiscal years), the 2nd to 4th surveys were conducted by the Tenri City Board of Education{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=1-4}}. * {{ill|2012|en|2012|WD=Q1990|lt=2012|1=2012}} ({{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|WD=Q234510|lt=Heisei|1=Heisei era}} 24): ** On April 9, an aerial 3D survey was conducted by the {{ill|The Museum, Archaeological Institute of Kashihara, Nara Prefecture|en|The Museum, Archaeological Institute of Kashihara, Nara Prefecture|WD=Q112961122|lt=Kashihara Archaeological Institute|1=The Museum, Archaeological Institute of Kashihara, Nara Prefecture}} and {{ill|Asia Aerial Surveying|ja|アジア航測|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Asia Aerial Surveying|1=Asia Air Survey|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11283384}}{{PDFlink|[http://www.ajiko.co.jp/news/2012/hashihaka_rittaichizu.pdf "Creation of a Red-colored 3D map of the Hashihaka and Seidenzuka Kofun"]}} (Press release from the Nara Prefectural Kashihara Archaeological Institute and Asia Aerial Surveying Co., Ltd., 2012).[https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXNASDG0503K_V00C12A6CR8000/ "Himiko’s Tomb? 3D Helicopter Survey of the Hashihaka Kofun by Kashihara Institute, etc."] (Nikkei, June 5, 2012).. ** In August, following a theft incident (with no destruction of the remains) and subsequent restoration, a survey was carried out by the {{ill|Archives and Mausolea Department|en|Archives and Mausolea Department|WD=Q4346533|lt=Archives and Mausolea Department|1=Archives and Mausolea Department}} {{Sfn|書陵部紀要 陵墓篇 第65号|2014|pp=108-112}}. * {{ill|2013|en|2013|WD=Q1998|lt=2013|1=2013}} ({{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|WD=Q234510|lt=Heisei|1=Heisei era}} 25) on February 20, an on-site survey was conducted by representatives of 15 academic societies in archaeology and history[https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXNASDG1905C_Q3A220C1CR0000/ "Himiko’s Tomb? First On-site Survey at the Hashihaka Kofun in Nara, Raising Expectations for Research Progress"] (Nikkei, February 20, 2013).. == Kofun == [[File:Tonotono-tsuka stereo.jpg|thumb|{{center|Nishitonozuka Kofun's {{ill|Stereogram|ja|ステレオグラム|lt=Stereogram|lt_ja=ステレオ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Stereogram|1=Stereogram|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1083936}} Aerial Photograph (1979) In the image, the {{ill|Higashidenzuka Kofun|ja|東殿塚古墳|1=Higashitonotsuka Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Higashidenzuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Higashitonotsuka Kofun|qq=}} is shown at the top and the {{ill|Seidenzuka Kofun|ja|西殿塚古墳|1=Nishitonozuka Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Seidenzuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitonozuka Kofun|qq=}} at the bottom. {{ill|National Aerial Photography|ja|国土航空写真|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Aerial Photography|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135491397|1=Geospatial Information Authority of Japan}}.]] The area of the tumulus are as follows{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=5-7}}. * Kofun length: approximately 230 meters (in some sources, 234 meters{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}, 220 meters{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 陵墓篇 第65号|2014|pp=108-112}}, or 219 meters{{R|堺市}}). * Posterior circular portion – built with 3 tiers on the east side and 4 tiers on the west side. ** Diameter: approximately 140 meters ** Height: approximately 16 meters (east side) * Anterior portion – built with 1 tier on the east side and 2 tiers on the west side. ** Width: approximately 130 meters ** Height: approximately 12 meters (east side) * Square plattype (mound) – built in one tier. ** Posterior circular portion: 25.15 meters east–west, 26.54 meters north–south, height 3.00 meters{{R|2012nd year 報道発表資料}} ** Anterior portion: 12.92 meters east–west, 14.43 meters north–south, height 1.87 meters{{R|2012nd year 報道発表資料}} In the theory where the tumulus length is taken as 219 meters, it Ranks as the 24th largest in the country{{R|堺市}}. The tiered terraces of the tumulus do not directly connect the posterior circular and anterior portions; the difference in tiers between these portions is reconciled in the constricted section{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991|pp=100-111}}. Furthermore, on the western side of the tumulus, a broad, flat surface (apron), characteristic of the Nishitonozuka Kofun, has been shaped as the lowest tier{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=5-7}}. On the eastern side of the tumulus, there are two bridge-like structures located in the central area of the posterior circular portion and on the southern side of the anterior portion, both of which connect to the adjacent {{ill|Higashidenzuka Kofun|ja|東殿塚古墳|1=Higashitonotsuka Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Higashidenzuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Higashitonotsuka Kofun|qq=}}{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=5-7}}. == Interred ==
'''Family Tree Based on the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|WD=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki|1=Nihon Shoki}}'''The reign intypeation is based on the {{ill|Nihon Jinmei Daijiten|ja|日本人名大辞典|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nihon Jinmei Daijiten|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Kodansha). {{familytree/start|style="text-align:left; font-size:100%"}} {{familytree|border=0|||||01| 01={{sup|24}} {{ill|Emperor Ninken|en|Emperor Ninken|WD=Q357266|lt=Emperor Ninken|1=Emperor Ninken}}
{{small|(Reign: end of 5th century)}}}} {{familytree|border=0|||||||)|.}} {{familytree|border=0|01|y|02|03| 01={{sup|26}} {{ill|Emperor Keitai|en|Emperor Keitai|WD=Q349277|lt=Emperor Keitai|1=Emperor Keitai}}
{{small|(Reign: 507?-531?)}}|02={{ill|Princess Tashiraka|en|Princess Tashiraka|WD=Q11075749|lt=Tebarakakōjo|1=Princess Tashiraka}}|03={{sup|25}} {{ill|Emperor Buretsu|en|Emperor Buretsu|WD=Q334644|lt=Emperor Buretsu|1=Emperor Buretsu}}
{{small|(Reign: end of 5th century – early 6th century)}}}} {{familytree|border=0||||01|| 01={{sup|29}} {{ill|Emperor Kinmei|en|Emperor Kinmei|WD=Q329792|lt=Emperor Kinmei|1=Emperor Kinmei}}
{{small|(Reign: 539?-571?)}}}} {{familytree/end}}
The actual interred of the {{ill|Seidenzuka Kofun|ja|西殿塚古墳|1=Nishitonozuka Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Seidenzuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitonozuka Kofun|qq=}} remains unclear; however, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} designates it as the mausoleum of the 26th {{ill|Emperor Keitai|en|Emperor Keitai|WD=Q349277|lt=Emperor Keitai|1=Emperor Keitai}}’s consort, '''{{ill|Princess Tashiraka|en|Princess Tashiraka|WD=Q11075749|lt=Tebarakakōjo|1=Princess Tashiraka}}''' (Tashiraka no Hime-miko, also rendered as Tashiraka no Hairarō/ Tashiraka no Himemi){{Sfn|衾田陵（国史）}}Compiled by the Imperial Ministry of Mausolea [{{NDLDC|1237123/11}} "Guide to Mausolea"] (1934, National Diet Library Digital Collection), 11 panels."Compilation of Mausoleum Topographical maps, Abbreviated Edition", compiled by the Imperial Household Agency Shoryo Department Mausoleum Section, [[Gakuseisha]], 2014, p. 406.. Although the mausoleum of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|en|Princess Tashiraka|WD=Q11075749|lt=Tebarakakōjo|1=Princess Tashiraka}} is not mentioned in either the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|WD=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki|1=Nihon Shoki}} or the {{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|WD=Q813031|lt=Kojiki|1=Kojiki}}, in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|Engishiki|WD=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki|1=Engishiki}}’s mausolea section (displayed as {{ill|Shoryo Department|ja|諸陵寮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shoryo Department|1=Shoryō-ryō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11632153}}) it is recorded as the distant "Kinuta Tomb". It is said to be located in {{ill|Yamato Province|en|Yamato Province|WD=Q907495|lt=Yamato Province|1=Yamato Province}}’s {{ill|Yamabe District, Nara|en|Yamabe District, Nara|WD=Q1130739|lt=Yamabe District|1=Yamabe District, Nara}}, covering an area of two chō east–west and two chō north–south, with no separate guard door, the mound door of the Kamikami Kofun of Yamabe (the mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|WD=Q333530|lt=Emperor Sushin|1=Emperor Sujin}}) concurrently serving as its guard{{Sfn|衾田陵（国史）}}. Later, during the {{ill|Middle Ages|en|Middle Ages|WD=Q12554|lt=Medieval period|1=Middle Ages}}, the traditional accounts regarding the location of the mausoleum were lost{{Sfn|衾田陵（国史）}}. In {{ill|1876|en|1876|WD=Q7766|lt=1876|1=1876}} ({{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era|1=Meiji era}} 9), the {{ill|Ministry of Religion (Japan)|en|Ministry of Religion (Japan)|WD=Q4294653|lt=Ministry of Religion|1=Ministry of Religion (Japan)}} Historic Site1 the {{ill|Seidenzuka Kofun|ja|西殿塚古墳|1=Nishitonozuka Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Seidenzuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitonozuka Kofun|qq=}} as the mausoleum, and in {{ill|1889|en|1889|WD=Q7831|lt=1889|1=1889}} ({{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era|1=Meiji era}} 22) repairs were carried out{{Sfn|衾田陵（国史）}}. [[File:Hashihaka-kofun zenkei.JPG|サムネイル|220px|{{center|{{ill|Hashihaka Kofun|en|Hashihaka Kofun|WD=Q11603420|lt=Hashihaka Kofun|1=Hashihaka Kofun}} (located in {{ill|Sakurai, Nara|en|Sakurai, Nara|WD=Q127026|lt=Sakurai City|1=Sakurai, Nara}}, Hashinaka)}}{{small|Attributed to {{ill|Princess Yamato Totohi Momoso|en|Princess Yamato Totohi Momoso|WD=Q11387098|lt=Wajishiki no Hime|1=Yamato-totohi-momoso-hime}}. Archaeologically, it is considered either the tomb of the first great king of the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|en|Yamato Kingship|WD=Q2658252|lt=Yamato Kingdom|1=Yamato Kingship}} or the tomb of {{ill|Himiko|en|Himiko|WD=Q234451|lt=Himiko|1=Himiko}}.}}]] On the other hand, regarding the true mausoleum of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|en|Princess Tashiraka|WD=Q11075749|lt=Tebarakakōjo|1=Princess Tashiraka}}, a prevailing theory holds that it should be identified not with the Nishitonozuka Kofun but with the {{ill|Nishiyamazuka Kofun|ja|西山塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishiyamazuka Kofun|qq=}} (located in Tenri City, Kayashō Town){{Sfn|天理の古墳100|2015|p=55}}. This theory is based on the fact that while the construction date of the Nishitonozuka Kofun is estimated to be around the latter half of the 3rd century, the date for the Nishiyamazuka Kofun is around the {{ill|6th century|en|6th century|WD=Q8090|lt=6th century|1=6th century}}, which corresponds with the assumed period for {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|en|Princess Tashiraka|WD=Q11075749|lt=Tebarakakōjo|1=Princess Tashiraka}}{{Sfn|天理の古墳100|2015|p=55}}. Meanwhile, as for the true interred of the Nishitonozuka Kofun, some theories propose that it is {{ill|Toyo (queen)|en|Toyo (queen)|WD=Q5358937|lt=Daiyo|1=Toyo (queen)}} (also written 壹與/臺與), based on its subsequent position to the {{ill|Hashihaka Kofun|en|Hashihaka Kofun|WD=Q11603420|lt=Hashihaka Kofun|1=Hashihaka Kofun}}—regarded as the tomb of {{ill|Himiko|en|Himiko|WD=Q234451|lt=Himiko|1=Himiko}}—or that it is {{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|WD=Q333530|lt=Emperor Sushin|1=Emperor Sujin}}{{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|1=Shiraishi Taichiro|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11580156}}, ''The Formation and Development of the Wa Kingdom as Seen from the Kofun'', Keibunsha, 2013, pp. 171-174.,{{ill|Suiz Wada|ja|和田萃|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suiz Wada|1=Atsumu Wada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11418120}} “On the Yamabe Road”, in ''The Ancient History of Mount Miwa'', Gakuseisha, 2003. among others. {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%" |+ Estimated Early Great King Tombs of the Yamato Kingdom
{{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|1=Shiraishi Taichiro|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11580156}}, ''The Formation and Development of the Wa Kingdom as Seen from the Kofun'' (日本歴史 私の最新講義), Keibunsha, 2013, pp. 181-186. ! Order !! Kofun name |- |1||{{ill|Hashihaka Kofun|en|Hashihaka Kofun|WD=Q11603420|lt=Hashihaka Kofun|1=Hashihaka Kofun}} |- |2||'''{{ill|Nishitonozuka Kofun|ja|西殿塚古墳|1=Nishitonozuka Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitonozuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitonozuka Kofun|qq=}}''' |- |3||{{ill|Sakurai Chausuyama Kofun|en|Sakurai Chausuyama Kofun|WD=Q11537882|lt=Sakurai Chausuyama Kofun|1=Sakurai Chausuyama Kofun}} |- |4||{{ill|Mesuriyama Kofun|en|Mesuriyama Kofun|WD=Q11343632|lt=Mesuriyama Kofun|1=Mesuriyama Kofun}} |- |5||{{ill|Andonyama Kofun|ja|行燈山古墳|1=Andon-yama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Andonyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Andon-yama Kofun|qq=}} |- |6||{{ill|Shibuya Mukaeyama Kofun|ja|渋谷向山古墳|1=Shibutani Mukoyama Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shibuya Mukaeyama Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Shibutani Mukoyama Kofun|qq=}} |} == References == {{Reflist|2}} == Further Reading == * Site explanation board, Tenri City Board of Education, 2010. * {{Cite book|和書|title=Nishitonozuka Kofun and Higashitonozuka Kofun (Tenri City Historic Site Report No.7)|publisher=Tenri City Board of Education|year=2000|ref={{Harvid|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|title=100 Kofun in Tenri|publisher=Tenri City Board of Education|year=2015|ref={{Harvid|天理の古墳100|2015}}}} == Related Articles == * {{ill|Ōyamato Kofun Cluster|ja|大和古墳群|1=Ōyamato Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamato Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamato Kofun Cluster|qq=}} * {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|en|Princess Tashiraka|WD=Q11075749|lt=Princess Tashiraka|1=Princess Tashiraka}} == External Links == * [http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/miryoku/tenrinomiryoku1/kofun/1445323092951.html Nishitonozuka Kofun - Considered the royal tomb following {{ill|Hashihaka Kofun|en|Hashihaka Kofun|WD=Q11603420|lt=Hashihaka Kofun|1=Hashihaka Kofun}} |map = Japan Nara |map_dot_label = Nishitonozuka Kofun |map_dot_label = Top |type = Keyhole-shaped tomb - South |architectural_styles = {{ill|keyhole-shaped kofun|WD=Q11268718|1=Zenpō-kōen-fun|2=ja|3=前方後円墳|4=ko|5=전방후원분|6=zh|7=前方後圓墳}} |commemorates = {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|WD=Q11075749|1=Princess Tashiraka}} }} [[File:Nishitonotsuka Kofun, haisho.jpg|thumb|220px|{{center|{{ill|Princess Tashiraka|en|Princess Tashiraka|WD=Q11075749|lt=Princess Tashiraka|1=Princess Tashiraka}} Fusumada Mausoleum {{ill|Haisho|ja|拝所|lt=Worship Site|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Haisho|qq=}}}}]] '''Nishitonozuka Kofun''' (西殿塚古墳) is a {{ill|Kofun|en|Kofun|WD=Q1141225|lt=Kofun|1=Kofun}} located in {{ill|Tenri, Nara|en|Tenri, Nara|WD=Q502196|lt=Tenri, Nara Prefecture|1=Tenri, Nara}}, Nakayama Town. It is a {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|en|Zenpō-kōen-fun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpō-kōen-fun|1=Zenpō-kōen-fun}} and part of the {{ill|Ōyamato Kofun Cluster|ja|大和古墳群|1=Ōyamato Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamato Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamato Kofun Cluster|qq=}} (Nakayama subgroup). The identity of the interred is uncertain, but the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} designates the site as the '''Fusumada Mausoleum''' (衾田陵), the resting place of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|en|Princess Tashiraka|WD=Q11075749|lt=Princess Tashiraka|1=Princess Tashiraka}}, the consort of {{ill|Emperor Keitai|en|Emperor Keitai|WD=Q349277|lt=Emperor Keitai|1=Emperor Keitai}} It is estimated to have been built in the latter half of the {{ill|3rd century|en|3rd century|WD=Q8101|lt=3rd century|1=3rd century}} (early {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|WD=Q459939|lt=Kofun period|1=Kofun period}}) and is considered the royal tomb succeeding the earliest keyhole-shaped tomb, the {{ill|Hashihaka Kofun|en|Hashihaka Kofun|WD=Q11603420|lt=Hashihaka Kofun|1=Hashihaka Kofun}}. == Overview == It is a gigantic keyhole-shaped tumulus constructed on the hilly area along the eastern edge of the {{ill|Nara Basin|en|Nara Basin|WD=Q10942269|lt=Nara Basin|1=Nara Basin}}. Adjacent to its eastern side is the {{ill|Higashitonotsuka Kofun|ja|東殿塚古墳|1=Higashitonotsuka Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Higashitonotsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Higashitonotsuka Kofun|qq=}}, and these two, being at the highest point within the {{ill|Ōyamato Kofun Cluster|ja|大和古墳群|1=Ōyamato Kofun Cluster|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamato Kofun Cluster|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōyamato Kofun Cluster|qq=}}, offer a panoramic view of the entire basinHistoric Site Explanation Board.{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 陵墓篇 第65号|2014|pp=108-112}}. The tumulus has remained well preserved to the present day{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991|pp=100-111}}. It is currently managed by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} as the mausoleum of an empress under its jurisdiction; to date, exterior investigations of the tumulus have been conducted by the {{ill|Archives and Mausolea Department|en|Archives and Mausolea Department|WD=Q4346533|lt=Archives and Mausolea Department|1=Archives and Mausolea Department}} during the {{ill|1989|en|1989|WD=Q2425|lt=1989|1=1989}} ({{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|WD=Q234510|lt=Heisei|1=Heisei era}} first fiscal year) period{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991|pp=100-111}}, surveys of the surrounding area by the Tenri City Board of Education during the {{ill|1992|en|1992|WD=Q2060|lt=1992|1=1992}}–{{ill|1994|en|1994|WD=Q2067|lt=1994|1=1994}} period (Heisei 4–6 fiscal years){{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=1-4}}, and an academic on-site survey in the {{ill|2012|en|2012|WD=Q1990|lt=2012|1=2012}} period (Heisei 24 fiscal year){{R|2013rd year 調査}}. The tumulus is of a keyhole type with its anterior portion facing south; however, because it was constructed at a right angle to a sloping terrain (with the higher elevation on the east side), it takes on an asymmetrical type{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}. In the posterior circular portion, it is built with three tiers on the east side and four tiers on the west side, while in the anterior portion it is built with one tier on the east side and two tiers on the west side{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=5-7}}. The overall length of the tumulus measures about 230 {{ill|Metre|en|Metre|WD=Q11573|lt=meters|1=Metre}}, making it the largest within the Ōyamato Kofun Cluster. On its exterior, in addition to the presence of {{ill|Fukiishi|en|Fukiishi|WD=Q11621213|lt=Fukiishi|1=Fukiishi}}, early haniwa have been detected around the tumulus, including {{ill|Special plattypes and jars|ja|特殊器台・特殊壺|1=Ceremonial vessel stands or jars|1=Ceremonial vessel stands or jars|lt=Special Kiderai-type earthenware, special Kiderai-type haniwa, special tsubo-shaped haniwa|lt_ja=特殊器台形土器・特殊器台形埴輪・特殊壺形埴輪|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Special plattypes and jars|13=User:Immanuelle/Ceremonial vessel stands or jars|qq=}} (from the tumulus itself) and {{ill|Cylindrical Haniwa|ja|円筒埴輪|lt=cylindrical haniwa|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Cylindrical Haniwa|qq=}} with a stepped neck{{R|説明板}}. Although the burial facilities remain unclear, square plattypes (mounds) are present on both the posterior and anterior portions of the tumulus{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=5-7}}. This Nishitonozuka Kofun is estimated to have been constructed in the latter half of the {{ill|3rd century|en|3rd century|WD=Q8101|lt=3rd century|1=3rd century}} during the early part of the {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|WD=Q459939|lt=Kofun period|1=Kofun period}}{{R|説明板}}[http://www.city.tenri.nara.jp/miryoku/tenrinomiryoku1/kofun/1445323092951.html]{{ill|Nishitonozuka Kofun|ja|西殿塚古墳|1=Nishitonozuka Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitonozuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitonozuka Kofun|qq=}} (Tenri City Homepage). It is regarded as the great tomb of the Yamato Kingdom that succeeded the {{ill|Hashihaka Kofun|en|Hashihaka Kofun|WD=Q11603420|lt=Hashihaka Kofun|1=Hashihaka Kofun}} (located in {{ill|Sakurai, Nara|en|Sakurai, Nara|WD=Q127026|lt=Sakurai City|1=Sakurai, Nara}} Hashinaka){{R|白石}}, and in conjunction with the adjacent {{ill|Higaida-ōtsuka Kofun|ja|東殿塚古墳|1=Higashitonotsuka Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Higaida-ōtsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Higashitonotsuka Kofun|qq=}}, it is considered to be part of a continuous construction sequence beginning with Nishitonozuka Kofun{{R|説明板}}. Although the identity of the interred remains unclear, it is currently Historic Site1 by the Imperial Household Agency as the mausoleum of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|en|Princess Tashiraka|WD=Q11075749|lt=Tebarakakōjo|1=Princess Tashiraka}} (the {{ill|Empress|ja|皇后|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Empress|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=Empress consort|WD=Q7723211}} of the 26th {{ill|Emperor Keitai|en|Emperor Keitai|WD=Q349277|lt=Emperor Keitai|1=Emperor Keitai}} ){{Sfn|衾田陵（国史）}}. However, since the construction date does not correspond with the assumed period of the {{ill|6th century|en|6th century|WD=Q8090|lt=6th century|1=6th century}} for {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|en|Princess Tashiraka|WD=Q11075749|lt=Tebarakakōjo|1=Princess Tashiraka}}, a theory that the true mausoleum of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|en|Princess Tashiraka|WD=Q11075749|lt=Tebarakakōjo|1=Princess Tashiraka}} is the {{ill|Nishiyamazuka Kofun|ja|西山塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishiyamazuka Kofun|qq=}} (in Tenri City, Kayashō Town) is strongly supported{{Sfn|天理の古墳100|2015|p=55}}, while alternative theories propose that the true interred of this tumulus is {{ill|Toyo (queen)|en|Toyo (queen)|WD=Q5358937|lt=Queen Toyo|1=Toyo (queen)}}, a successor to {{ill|Himiko|en|Himiko|WD=Q234451|lt=Himiko|1=Himiko}} (who may have been enshrined in the Hashihaka Kofun){{R|白石}}. == burial == The interred individual is not definitively known, but the site is officially Historic Site1 as the resting place of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|en|Princess Tashiraka|WD=Q11075749|lt=Princess Tashiraka|1=Princess Tashiraka}}. However, the construction date (3rd century) conflicts with Princess Tashiraka’s presumed era (6th century), leading some to propose the nearby {{ill|Nishiyamazuka Kofun|ja|西山塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishiyamazuka Kofun|qq=}} as her true mausoleum.{{Sfn|天理の古墳100|2015|p=55}} Other theories suggest Queen {{ill|Himiko|en|Himiko|WD=Q234451|lt=Himiko|1=Himiko}}’s successor, {{ill|Toyo (queen)|en|Toyo (queen)|WD=Q5358937|lt=Queen Toyo|1=Toyo (queen)}}, or {{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|WD=Q333530|lt=Emperor Sujin|1=Emperor Sujin}} as the interred individual.{{Sfn|白石太一郎|2013|pp=171-174}} == Site History == * {{ill|1876|en|1876|WD=Q7766|lt=1876|1=1876}} ({{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era|1=Meiji era}} 9), Historic Site1 as the mausoleum of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|en|Princess Tashiraka|WD=Q11075749|lt=Tebarakakōjo|1=Princess Tashiraka}}{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 陵墓篇 第65号|2014|pp=108-112}}. * {{ill|1889|en|1889|WD=Q7831|lt=1889|1=1889}} ({{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era|1=Meiji era}} 22), repaired and maintained as a mausoleum {{ill|Kinuta Tomb|ja|衾田陵（国史）|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kinuta Tomb|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. * {{ill|1986|en|1986|WD=Q2430|lt=1986|1=1986}} period ({{ill|Shōwa era|en|Shōwa era|WD=Q327567|lt=Shōwa|1=Shōwa era}} 61 fiscal year), the first survey was conducted{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=1-4}}. * {{ill|1989|en|1989|WD=Q2425|lt=1989|1=1989}} period ({{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|WD=Q234510|lt=Heisei|1=Heisei era}} first fiscal year), an exterior survey of the tumulus was carried out by the {{ill|Archives and Mausolea Department|en|Archives and Mausolea Department|WD=Q4346533|lt=Archives and Mausolea Department|1=Archives and Mausolea Department}} {{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991|pp=100-111}}. * From {{ill|1992|en|1992|WD=Q2060|lt=1992|1=1992}} to {{ill|1994|en|1994|WD=Q2067|lt=1994|1=1994}}, ({{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|WD=Q234510|lt=Heisei|1=Heisei era}} 4–6 fiscal years), the 2nd to 4th surveys were conducted by the Tenri City Board of Education{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=1-4}}. * {{ill|2012|en|2012|WD=Q1990|lt=2012|1=2012}} ({{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|WD=Q234510|lt=Heisei|1=Heisei era}} 24): ** On April 9, an aerial 3D survey was conducted by the {{ill|The Museum, Archaeological Institute of Kashihara, Nara Prefecture|en|The Museum, Archaeological Institute of Kashihara, Nara Prefecture|WD=Q112961122|lt=Kashihara Archaeological Institute|1=The Museum, Archaeological Institute of Kashihara, Nara Prefecture}} and {{ill|Asia Aerial Surveying|ja|アジア航測|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Asia Aerial Surveying|1=Asia Air Survey|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11283384}}{{PDFlink|[http://www.ajiko.co.jp/news/2012/hashihaka_rittaichizu.pdf "Creation of a Red-colored 3D map of the Hashihaka and Seidenzuka Kofun"]}} (Press release from the Nara Prefectural Kashihara Archaeological Institute and Asia Aerial Surveying Co., Ltd., 2012).[https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXNASDG0503K_V00C12A6CR8000/ "Himiko’s Tomb? 3D Helicopter Survey of the Hashihaka Kofun by Kashihara Institute, etc."] (Nikkei, June 5, 2012).. ** In August, following a theft incident (with no destruction of the remains) and subsequent restoration, a survey was carried out by the {{ill|Archives and Mausolea Department|en|Archives and Mausolea Department|WD=Q4346533|lt=Archives and Mausolea Department|1=Archives and Mausolea Department}} {{Sfn|書陵部紀要 陵墓篇 第65号|2014|pp=108-112}}. * {{ill|2013|en|2013|WD=Q1998|lt=2013|1=2013}} ({{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|WD=Q234510|lt=Heisei|1=Heisei era}} 25) on February 20, an on-site survey was conducted by representatives of 15 academic societies in archaeology and history[https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXNASDG1905C_Q3A220C1CR0000/ "Himiko’s Tomb? First On-site Survey at the Hashihaka Kofun in Nara, Raising Expectations for Research Progress"] (Nikkei, February 20, 2013).. == Kofun == [[File:Tonotono-tsuka stereo.jpg|thumb|{{center|Nishitonozuka Kofun's {{ill|Stereogram|ja|ステレオグラム|lt=Stereogram|lt_ja=ステレオ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Stereogram|1=Stereogram|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q1083936}} Aerial Photograph (1979) In the image, the {{ill|Higashidenzuka Kofun|ja|東殿塚古墳|1=Higashitonotsuka Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Higashidenzuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Higashitonotsuka Kofun|qq=}} is shown at the top and the {{ill|Seidenzuka Kofun|ja|西殿塚古墳|1=Nishitonozuka Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Seidenzuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitonozuka Kofun|qq=}} at the bottom. {{ill|National Aerial Photography|ja|国土航空写真|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/National Aerial Photography|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|WD=Q135491397|1=Geospatial Information Authority of Japan}}.]] The area of the tumulus are as follows{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=5-7}}. * Kofun length: approximately 230 meters (in some sources, 234 meters{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳（古墳）|1989}}, 220 meters{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 陵墓篇 第65号|2014|pp=108-112}}, or 219 meters{{R|堺市}}). * Posterior circular portion – built with 3 tiers on the east side and 4 tiers on the west side. ** Diameter: approximately 140 meters ** Height: approximately 16 meters (east side) * Anterior portion – built with 1 tier on the east side and 2 tiers on the west side. ** Width: approximately 130 meters ** Height: approximately 12 meters (east side) * Square plattype (mound) – built in one tier. ** Posterior circular portion: 25.15 meters east–west, 26.54 meters north–south, height 3.00 meters{{R|2012nd year 報道発表資料}} ** Anterior portion: 12.92 meters east–west, 14.43 meters north–south, height 1.87 meters{{R|2012nd year 報道発表資料}} In the theory where the tumulus length is taken as 219 meters, it Ranks as the 24th largest in the country{{R|堺市}}. The tiered terraces of the tumulus do not directly connect the posterior circular and anterior portions; the difference in tiers between these portions is reconciled in the constricted section{{Sfn|書陵部紀要 第42号|1991|pp=100-111}}. Furthermore, on the western side of the tumulus, a broad, flat surface (apron), characteristic of the Nishitonozuka Kofun, has been shaped as the lowest tier{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=5-7}}. On the eastern side of the tumulus, there are two bridge-like structures located in the central area of the posterior circular portion and on the southern side of the anterior portion, both of which connect to the adjacent {{ill|Higashidenzuka Kofun|ja|東殿塚古墳|1=Higashitonotsuka Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Higashidenzuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Higashitonotsuka Kofun|qq=}}{{Sfn|西殿塚古墳・東殿塚古墳|2000|pp=5-7}}. == Interred ==
'''Family Tree Based on the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|WD=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki|1=Nihon Shoki}}'''The reign intypeation is based on the {{ill|Nihon Jinmei Daijiten|ja|日本人名大辞典|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nihon Jinmei Daijiten|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Kodansha). {{familytree/start|style="text-align:left; font-size:100%"}} {{familytree|border=0|||||01| 01={{sup|24}} {{ill|Emperor Ninken|en|Emperor Ninken|WD=Q357266|lt=Emperor Ninken|1=Emperor Ninken}}
{{small|(Reign: end of 5th century)}}}} {{familytree|border=0|||||||)|.}} {{familytree|border=0|01|y|02|03| 01={{sup|26}} {{ill|Emperor Keitai|en|Emperor Keitai|WD=Q349277|lt=Emperor Keitai|1=Emperor Keitai}}
{{small|(Reign: 507?-531?)}}|02={{ill|Princess Tashiraka|en|Princess Tashiraka|WD=Q11075749|lt=Tebarakakōjo|1=Princess Tashiraka}}|03={{sup|25}} {{ill|Emperor Buretsu|en|Emperor Buretsu|WD=Q334644|lt=Emperor Buretsu|1=Emperor Buretsu}}
{{small|(Reign: end of 5th century – early 6th century)}}}} {{familytree|border=0||||01|| 01={{sup|29}} {{ill|Emperor Kinmei|en|Emperor Kinmei|WD=Q329792|lt=Emperor Kinmei|1=Emperor Kinmei}}
{{small|(Reign: 539?-571?)}}}} {{familytree/end}}
The actual interred of the {{ill|Seidenzuka Kofun|ja|西殿塚古墳|1=Nishitonozuka Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Seidenzuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitonozuka Kofun|qq=}} remains unclear; however, the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency|en|Imperial Household Agency|WD=Q1143602|lt=Imperial Household Agency|1=Imperial Household Agency}} designates it as the mausoleum of the 26th {{ill|Emperor Keitai|en|Emperor Keitai|WD=Q349277|lt=Emperor Keitai|1=Emperor Keitai}}’s consort, '''{{ill|Princess Tashiraka|en|Princess Tashiraka|WD=Q11075749|lt=Tebarakakōjo|1=Princess Tashiraka}}''' (Tashiraka no Hime-miko, also rendered as Tashiraka no Hairarō/ Tashiraka no Himemi){{Sfn|衾田陵（国史）}}Compiled by the Imperial Ministry of Mausolea [{{NDLDC|1237123/11}} "Guide to Mausolea"] (1934, National Diet Library Digital Collection), 11 panels."Compilation of Mausoleum Topographical maps, Abbreviated Edition", compiled by the Imperial Household Agency Shoryo Department Mausoleum Section, [[Gakuseisha]], 2014, p. 406.. Although the mausoleum of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|en|Princess Tashiraka|WD=Q11075749|lt=Tebarakakōjo|1=Princess Tashiraka}} is not mentioned in either the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|WD=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki|1=Nihon Shoki}} or the {{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|WD=Q813031|lt=Kojiki|1=Kojiki}}, in the {{ill|Engishiki|en|Engishiki|WD=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki|1=Engishiki}}’s mausolea section (displayed as {{ill|Shoryo Department|ja|諸陵寮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shoryo Department|1=Shoryō-ryō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11632153}}) it is recorded as the distant "Kinuta Tomb". It is said to be located in {{ill|Yamato Province|en|Yamato Province|WD=Q907495|lt=Yamato Province|1=Yamato Province}}’s {{ill|Yamabe District, Nara|en|Yamabe District, Nara|WD=Q1130739|lt=Yamabe District|1=Yamabe District, Nara}}, covering an area of two chō east–west and two chō north–south, with no separate guard door, the mound door of the Kamikami Kofun of Yamabe (the mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|WD=Q333530|lt=Emperor Sushin|1=Emperor Sujin}}) concurrently serving as its guard{{Sfn|衾田陵（国史）}}. Later, during the {{ill|Middle Ages|en|Middle Ages|WD=Q12554|lt=Medieval period|1=Middle Ages}}, the traditional accounts regarding the location of the mausoleum were lost{{Sfn|衾田陵（国史）}}. In {{ill|1876|en|1876|WD=Q7766|lt=1876|1=1876}} ({{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era|1=Meiji era}} 9), the {{ill|Ministry of Religion (Japan)|en|Ministry of Religion (Japan)|WD=Q4294653|lt=Ministry of Religion|1=Ministry of Religion (Japan)}} Historic Site1 the {{ill|Seidenzuka Kofun|ja|西殿塚古墳|1=Nishitonozuka Kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Seidenzuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishitonozuka Kofun|qq=}} as the mausoleum, and in {{ill|1889|en|1889|WD=Q7831|lt=1889|1=1889}} ({{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era|1=Meiji era}} 22) repairs were carried out{{Sfn|衾田陵（国史）}}. [[File:Hashihaka-kofun zenkei.JPG|サムネイル|220px|{{center|{{ill|Hashihaka Kofun|en|Hashihaka Kofun|WD=Q11603420|lt=Hashihaka Kofun|1=Hashihaka Kofun}} (located in {{ill|Sakurai, Nara|en|Sakurai, Nara|WD=Q127026|lt=Sakurai City|1=Sakurai, Nara}}, Hashinaka)}}{{small|Attributed to {{ill|Princess Yamato Totohi Momoso|en|Princess Yamato Totohi Momoso|WD=Q11387098|lt=Wajishiki no Hime|1=Yamato-totohi-momoso-hime}}. Archaeologically, it is considered either the tomb of the first great king of the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|en|Yamato Kingship|WD=Q2658252|lt=Yamato Kingdom|1=Yamato Kingship}} or the tomb of {{ill|Himiko|en|Himiko|WD=Q234451|lt=Himiko|1=Himiko}}.}}]] On the other hand, regarding the true mausoleum of {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|en|Princess Tashiraka|WD=Q11075749|lt=Tebarakakōjo|1=Princess Tashiraka}}, a prevailing theory holds that it should be identified not with the Nishitonozuka Kofun but with the {{ill|Nishiyamazuka Kofun|ja|西山塚古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nishiyamazuka Kofun|qq=}} (located in Tenri City, Kayashō Town){{Sfn|天理の古墳100|2015|p=55}}. This theory is based on the fact that while the construction date of the Nishitonozuka Kofun is estimated to be around the latter half of the 3rd century, the date for the Nishiyamazuka Kofun is around the {{ill|6th century|en|6th century|WD=Q8090|lt=6th century|1=6th century}}, which corresponds with the assumed period for {{ill|Princess Tashiraka|en|Princess Tashiraka|WD=Q11075749|lt=Tebarakakōjo|1=Princess Tashiraka}}{{Sfn|天理の古墳100|2015|p=55}}. Meanwhile, as for the true interred of the Nishitonozuka Kofun, some theories propose that it is {{ill|Toyo (queen)|en|Toyo (queen)|WD=Q5358937|lt=Daiyo|1=Toyo (queen)}} (also written 壹與/臺與), based on its subsequent position to the {{ill|Hashihaka Kofun|en|Hashihaka Kofun|WD=Q11603420|lt=Hashihaka Kofun|1=Hashihaka Kofun}}—regarded as the tomb of {{ill|Himiko|en|Himiko|WD=Q234451|lt=Himiko|1=Himiko}}—or that it is {{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|WD=Q333530|lt=Emperor Sushin|1=Emperor Sujin}}{{ill|Taichirō Shiraishi|ja|白石太一郎|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taichirō Shiraishi|1=Shiraishi Taichiro|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11580156}}, ''The Formation and Development of the Wa Kingdom as Seen from the Kofun'', Keibunsha, 2013, pp. 171-174.,{{ill|Suiz Wada|ja|和田萃|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suiz Wada|1=Atsumu Wada|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11418120}} “On the Yamabe Road”, in ''The Ancient History of Mount Miwa'', Gakuseisha, 2003. among others. {| class="wikitable" style="background:#ffffff;text-align:center;font-size:85%" |+ Estimated Early Great King Tombs of the Yamato Kingdom
